title.zh: 卷五十六 列傳第四十六 張弘策 庾域 鄭紹叔 呂僧珍 樂藹
title.en: Volume 56 Biographies 46: Zhang Hongce, Yu Yu, Zheng Shaoshu, Lu Sengzhen, Le Ai
title.raw: 卷五十六 列傳第四十六 張弘策 庾域 鄭紹叔 呂僧珍 樂藹 Volume 56 Biographies 46: Zhang Hongce, Yu Yu, Zheng Shaoshu, Lu Sengzhen, Le Ai

sentences.zh: 列傳第四十六

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Forty-Six.
translations.idiomatic: the 46th year of Biographies

sentences.zh: 張弘策庾域鄭紹叔呂僧珍樂藹

translations.literal: Zhang Hongce, Yu Yu, Zheng Shaoshu, Lu Sengzhen, and Le Ai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hongce, Yu Yu, Zheng Shaoshu, Lu Sengzhen, and Le Ai

sentences.zh: 張弘策字真簡，范陽方城人，梁文獻皇后之從父弟也。

translations.literal: Zhang Hongce, courtesy name Zhenjian, was a native of Fangcheng in Fanyang and a younger cousin of Empress Wenxian of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hongce, courtesy name Zhenjian, was a native of Fangcheng in Fanyang and a younger cousin of Empress Wenxian of Liang.

sentences.zh: 父安之，青州主簿、南蠻行參軍。

translations.literal: His father Anzhi served as chief clerk of Qingzhou and acting staff officer of the Southern Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: His father Anzhi served as chief clerk of Qingzhou and acting Southern Barbarians staff officer.

sentences.zh: 弘策幼以孝聞，母嘗有疾，五日不食，弘策亦不食。

translations.literal: Hongce was known from childhood for filial piety; when his mother once fell ill, for five days she did not eat, and Hongce also did not eat.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Hongce was famed for filial devotion. When his mother once fell ill, she went five days without food, and Hongce refused to eat as well.

sentences.zh: 母強為進粥，弘策乃食母所餘。

translations.literal: His mother forced herself to take gruel; Hongce then ate what his mother had left over.
translations.idiomatic: When she was pressed to take some gruel, Hongce would eat only what she had left in the bowl.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，三年不食鹽菜，幾至滅性。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death he observed mourning; for three years he ate neither salt nor vegetables, nearly destroying himself.
translations.idiomatic: After her death he observed the full mourning rites and for three years took no salted or seasoned food, coming close to wasting away.

sentences.zh: 兄弟友愛，不忍暫離。

translations.literal: He and his brothers were affectionate and could not bear to part even briefly.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers were deeply devoted to one another and could hardly bear to be apart even for a moment.

sentences.zh: 雖各有室，常同臥起，世比之姜肱兄弟。

translations.literal: Although each had his own household, they regularly slept and rose together; the age compared them to the brothers Jiang Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Though each had married and set up his own household, they still slept and rose together; people compared them to the famed Jiang Gong brothers.

sentences.zh: 弘策與梁武帝年相輩，幼見親狎，恒隨帝遊處。

translations.literal: Hongce was about the same age as the future Emperor Wu of Liang; from youth they were intimate, and he constantly followed the Emperor in his comings and goings.
translations.idiomatic: Hongce was nearly the same age as the future Liang Emperor Wu; they had been close since childhood, and Hongce was always at his side wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 每入室，常覺有雲氣，體輒肅然，弘策由此特加敬異。

translations.literal: Whenever he entered a room, he would often sense a cloudlike aura; his body would grow solemn, and for this reason Hongce treated him with special reverence and wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he entered a room Hongce sensed something like a clouded aura about him and felt himself grow solemn; from this Hongce came to regard him with especial awe.

sentences.zh: 建武末，與兄弘胄從武帝宿，酒酣，移席星下，語及時事。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jianwu era, together with his elder brother Hongzhou he kept vigil with the future Emperor; when the wine had warmed them, they moved their mats beneath the stars and spoke of current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Jianwu period he and his brother Hongzhou stayed the night with the future Emperor; when the wine had taken hold they carried their mats out under the stars to discuss the times.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「天下方亂，舅知之乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "The realm is in turmoil—does my uncle know this?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "The realm is in turmoil. Uncle, do you see it?

sentences.zh: 冬下魏軍方動，則亡漢北。

translations.literal: When winter comes and the Wei armies stir, the north of Han will perish.
translations.idiomatic: When winter comes and the Wei armies move, the north of Han will fall.

sentences.zh: 王敬則猜嫌已久，當乘間而作。」

translations.literal: Wang Jingze has long harbored suspicion and resentment; he will seize an opening to act."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingze has long nursed suspicion and resentment; he will strike when he sees his chance."

sentences.zh: 弘策曰：「敬則張兩赤眼，容能立事？」

translations.literal: Hongce said, "Jingze opens his two red eyes wide—can he really accomplish anything?"
translations.idiomatic: Hongce said, "Jingze only glares with those bloodshot eyes—can he really pull anything off?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「敬則庸才，為天下唱先爾。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Jingze is a mediocrity; he will merely be the first in the realm to raise the cry.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Jingze is a mediocrity; he will only be the first in the realm to sound the alarm.

sentences.zh: 主上運祚盡于來年，國權當歸江、劉。

translations.literal: Our lord's mandate will run out next year, and state power will pass to the Jiang and Liu clans.
translations.idiomatic: The throne's mandate will expire next year, and power will pass to the Jiang and Liu factions.

sentences.zh: 而江甚隘，劉又闇弱，都下當大亂，死人如亂麻。

translations.literal: Yet Jiang is very narrow-minded, and Liu is both dim and weak; the capital will see great chaos, with the dead heaped like tangled hemp.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jiang is narrow-minded, and Liu is both dull and weak; the capital will erupt in chaos, and the dead will pile up like tangled hemp.

sentences.zh: 齊之歷數自茲亡矣。

translations.literal: The dynastic fortune of Qi will from this moment be extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: From that point the dynastic fortune of Qi will be spent.

sentences.zh: 梁、楚、漢當有英雄興。」

translations.literal: In Liang, Chu, and Han heroes will rise."
translations.idiomatic: Heroes will rise in the regions of Liang, Chu, and Han."

sentences.zh: 弘策曰：「瞻烏爰止，於誰之屋？」

translations.literal: Hongce said, "The crow looks about—on whose roof will it alight?"
translations.idiomatic: Hongce said, "The crow looks about—whose roof will it choose?"

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「光武所雲，'安知非僕'。」

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed and said, "As Guangwu said: 'How do you know it will not be I?'
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor laughed and said, "As Emperor Guangwu put it: 'How do you know it will not be me?'"

sentences.zh: 弘策起曰：「今夜之言，是天意也，請定君臣之分。」

translations.literal: Hongce rose and said, "Tonight's words are Heaven's intent; please fix the distinction between ruler and minister."
translations.idiomatic: Hongce rose and said, "What we have said tonight is Heaven's will. Let us settle the bond between ruler and minister."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「舅欲斅鄧晨乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Does my uncle wish to play Deng Chen to me?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Uncle, do you mean to play Deng Chen to my Liu Xiu?"

sentences.zh: 是冬，魏軍攻新野，齊明帝密詔武帝代曹武監雍州事。

translations.literal: That winter the Wei army attacked Xinye; Emperor Ming of Qi secretly ordered the future Emperor to replace Cao Wu in supervising Yong Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, as the Wei army attacked Xinye, Emperor Ming of Qi secretly ordered the future Emperor to replace Cao Wu and take charge of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 弘策聞之心喜，謂帝曰：「夜中言當驗。」

translations.literal: Hongce heard this with joy in his heart and said to the Emperor, "What was said at night will surely be fulfilled."
translations.idiomatic: Hongce was overjoyed and said to the Emperor, "What we said that night is already coming true."

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「且勿多言。」

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed and said, "Say no more for now."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor laughed and said, "Enough talk for now."

sentences.zh: 弘策從帝西行，仍參帷幄，身親勞役，不憚辛苦。

translations.literal: Hongce followed the Emperor west, still taking part in the command tent; he personally shared in the labor and did not shrink from hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Hongce followed the Emperor west, still serving in the command tent; he shared personally in the labor and never flinched from hardship.

sentences.zh: 齊明帝崩，遺詔以帝為雍州刺史，乃表弘策為錄事參軍，帶襄陽令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming of Qi died, his final edict appointed the future Emperor Governor of Yong Province; he then memorialized to appoint Hongce Recorder-General and acting magistrate of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming of Qi died, his final edict made the future Emperor Governor of Yong Province; the Emperor then recommended Hongce as Recorder-General with concurrent duties as magistrate of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 帝觀海內方亂，有匡濟之心，密為儲備。

translations.literal: The Emperor saw that the realm was falling into chaos and harbored a mind to set things right; he secretly made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the realm sliding into chaos, the Emperor resolved to restore order and began making secret preparations.

sentences.zh: 謀猷所及，唯弘策而已。

translations.literal: In planning and counsel he relied on none but Hongce.
translations.idiomatic: In all his planning he confided in no one but Hongce.

sentences.zh: 時帝長兄懿罷益州還，為西中郎長史、行郢州事。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor's eldest brother Yi, having left his post in Yizhou, returned and served as chief clerk to the General of the West and acting administrator of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Emperor's eldest brother Yi had returned from Yizhou and was serving as chief clerk to the General of the West with acting authority over Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 帝使弘策到郢，陳計於懿曰：「昔晉惠庸主，諸王爭權，遂內難九興，外寇三作。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Hongce to Ying to lay out a plan to Yi, saying, "In the past Emperor Hui of Jin was a mediocre ruler; the princes fought for power, and so internal strife arose nine times and foreign invasions three times.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Hongce to Ying to lay out a plan to Yi: "In the past Emperor Hui of Jin was a mediocre ruler; the princes fought for power, internal strife broke out nine times, and foreign invasions came three times.

sentences.zh: 方今喪亂有甚於此，六貴爭權，人握王憲，制主畫敕，各欲專成。

translations.literal: Today disorder is worse than that: the six nobles contend for power; each man holds the royal writ, drafts edicts for the ruler, and wishes to have his own way.
translations.idiomatic: Today's disorder is worse still: the six powerful ministers vie for power; each holds the royal writ, drafts edicts for the throne, and wants his own will to prevail.

sentences.zh: 且嗣主在宮本無令譽，媟近左右，蜂目忍人。

translations.literal: Moreover the heir in the palace had no good reputation to begin with; he is familiar with those at his side, with bee-like eyes and a cruel heart.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the heir apparent had never enjoyed a good reputation; he is intimate with his attendants, with bee-like eyes and a cruel disposition.

sentences.zh: 一居萬機，恣其所欲，豈肯虛坐主諾，委政朝臣。

translations.literal: Once he holds the myriad affairs of state, he will indulge his every desire—how could he sit idly as nominal master while leaving government to the court ministers?
translations.idiomatic: Once he holds the reins of power he will indulge every whim—how could he sit as a figurehead while leaving affairs to the court?

sentences.zh: 積相嫌貳，必大誅戮。

translations.literal: As mutual suspicion builds, there will surely be great slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: As suspicion mounts between them, a great bloodletting is sure to follow.

sentences.zh: 始安欲為趙倫，形跡已露，蹇人上天，信無此理。

translations.literal: Shi'an wishes to play Zhao Lun; his intentions are already exposed—a lame man climbing to Heaven truly has no such prospect.
translations.idiomatic: Shi'an wants to play the part of Zhao Lun; his designs are already plain—a lame man climbing to Heaven is simply not in the cards.

sentences.zh: 且性甚猜狹，徒取禍機，所可當軸，江、劉而已。

translations.literal: Moreover his nature is very suspicious and narrow; he will only invite disaster. Those fit to hold the pivot of power are only Jiang and Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he is deeply suspicious and narrow-minded and will only court disaster. Those fit to hold real power are Jiang and Liu alone.

sentences.zh: 祏怯而無斷，暄弱而不才，折鼎覆餗，跂踵可待。

translations.literal: Jiang Shi is timid and indecisive; Liu Xuan is weak and without talent—the cauldron will break and the stew spill; one need only stand on tiptoe and wait.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shi is timid and indecisive; Liu Xuan is weak and incompetent—the cauldron will break and the stew spill; disaster waits only a step away.

sentences.zh: 蕭坦胸懷猜忌，動言相傷。

translations.literal: Xiao Tan harbors suspicion in his breast and at every turn speaks words that wound others.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Tan is full of suspicion and at every turn speaks words meant to wound.

sentences.zh: 徐孝嗣才非柱石，聽人穿鼻。

translations.literal: Xu Xiaosi's talent is not that of a pillar of state; he lets others lead him by the nose.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xiaosi lacks the stature of a pillar of state; he lets others lead him by the nose.

sentences.zh: 若隙開釁起，必中外土崩。

translations.literal: If a rift opens and trouble begins, court and countryside will surely crumble like earth in collapse.
translations.idiomatic: If a breach opens and trouble flares, court and countryside alike will collapse.

sentences.zh: 今得外藩，幸圖身計。

translations.literal: Now that you hold an outer commandery, you are fortunate to be able to plan for your own safety.
translations.idiomatic: Now that you hold an outer command, you are fortunate enough to plan for your own safety.

sentences.zh: 及今猜防未生，宜召諸弟，以時聚集。

translations.literal: Before suspicion and guard arise, you should summon your younger brothers and gather them in good time.
translations.idiomatic: Before suspicion and watchfulness arise, you should summon your younger brothers and gather them while there is still time.

sentences.zh: 郢州控帶荊、湘，西注漢、沔。

translations.literal: Ying Province commands Jing and Xiang and pours westward into the Han and Mian rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Province commands Jing and Xiang and opens westward onto the Han and Mian rivers.

sentences.zh: 雍州士馬，呼吸數萬。

translations.literal: Yong Province's soldiers and horses number in the tens of thousands at a breath.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Province can field tens of thousands of troops at a moment's notice.

sentences.zh: 時安則竭誠本朝，時亂則為國翦暴，如不早圖，悔無及也。」

translations.literal: In peace you may devote yourself wholly to the court; in chaos you may cut down the violent for the state—if you do not plan early, regret will come too late."
translations.idiomatic: In peace you can serve the court with full loyalty; in chaos you can strike down the violent for the realm—if you do not act now, it will be too late for regret."

sentences.zh: 懿聞之變色，心未之許。

translations.literal: Yi heard this and changed color, but in his heart he did not assent.
translations.idiomatic: Yi heard this and turned pale, but in his heart he would not agree.

sentences.zh: 及懿遇禍，帝將起兵，夜召弘策、呂僧珍入定議，旦乃發兵。

translations.literal: When Yi met with disaster, the Emperor was about to raise troops; at night he summoned Hongce and Lu Sengzhen into the inner council to deliberate, and at dawn he set out his army.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi met disaster, the Emperor prepared to raise troops; he summoned Hongce and Lu Sengzhen at night for a council in the inner quarters and marched at dawn.

sentences.zh: 以弘策為輔國將軍、軍主，領萬人督後部事。

translations.literal: He appointed Hongce General Who Supports the State and army commander, leading ten thousand men to oversee rear affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He made Hongce General Who Supports the State and army commander, putting ten thousand men under him to oversee the rear.

sentences.zh: 及郢城平，蕭穎達、楊公則諸將皆欲頓軍夏口，帝以為宜乘勝長驅，直指建鄴，弘策與帝意合。

translations.literal: When Ying city was pacified, the generals Xiao Yingda, Yang Gongze, and others all wished to halt the army at Xiakou; the Emperor thought they should press the victory in a long drive straight at Jiankang, and Hongce agreed with the Emperor's view.
translations.idiomatic: After Ying fell, generals such as Xiao Yingda and Yang Gongze all wanted to halt at Xiakou; the Emperor favored pressing the victory in a long drive straight at Jiankang, and Hongce agreed with him.

sentences.zh: 又訪甯朔將軍庾域，域又同。

translations.literal: He also consulted the General Who Pacifies the North, Yu Yu, and Yu likewise agreed.
translations.idiomatic: He also consulted General Who Pacifies the North Yu Yu, who agreed as well.

sentences.zh: 即日上道，凡磯浦、村落，軍行宿次，立頓處所，弘策預為圖，皆在目中。

translations.literal: That very day they took the road; every shoal, harbor, village, and hamlet—where the army marched, encamped, or halted—Hongce had mapped in advance, all clear before his eyes.
translations.idiomatic: That very day they marched. Every shoal, harbor, village, and halt along the route Hongce had mapped in advance; nothing escaped his eye.

sentences.zh: 城平，帝遣弘策與呂僧珍先往清宮，封檢府庫。

translations.literal: When the city was pacified, the Emperor sent Hongce and Lu Sengzhen ahead to clear the palace, seal and inspect the treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, the Emperor sent Hongce and Lu Sengzhen ahead to secure the palace and seal the treasuries for inspection.

sentences.zh: 于時城內珍寶委積，弘策申勒部曲，秋毫無犯。

translations.literal: At that time treasures were heaped within the city; Hongce sternly charged his troops, and not the slightest thing was violated.
translations.idiomatic: Treasures lay heaped throughout the city; Hongce sternly charged his men, and not the slightest thing was touched.

sentences.zh: 遷衛尉卿，加給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Guards and additionally made Attendant Within the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of the Guards with the additional title Attendant Within the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 天監初，加散騎常侍，封洮陽縣侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he was further made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and enfeoffed as Marquis of Taoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianjian reign he was made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and enfeoffed as Marquis of Taoyang.

sentences.zh: 弘策盡忠奉上，知無不為，交友故舊，隨才薦拔，縉紳皆趨焉。

translations.literal: Hongce served the throne with full loyalty and did all he knew how; among friends and old associates he promoted men according to their talents, and the gentry all flocked to him.
translations.idiomatic: Hongce served with full loyalty and held nothing back; among friends and old associates he promoted men according to talent, and the gentry all flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 時東昏餘党孫文明等初逢赦令，多未自安。

translations.literal: At that time Sun Wenming and other remnants of Dong Hun's faction had just received an amnesty and for the most part did not feel secure.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Sun Wenming and other remnants of Dong Hun's faction had just been amnestied and for the most part still felt uneasy.

sentences.zh: 文明又嘗夢乘馬至雲龍門，心惑其夢，遂作亂。

translations.literal: Wenming had also once dreamed of riding a horse to the Cloud Dragon Gate; his heart was troubled by the dream, and so he raised a rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Wenming had also dreamed of riding a horse to the Cloud Dragon Gate; troubled by the dream, he rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 帥數百人，因運荻炬束仗，得入南、北掖門，至夜燒神獸門、總章觀，入衛尉府，弘策踰垣匿于龍廄，遇賊見害。

translations.literal: He led several hundred men and, under cover of transporting reed torches and bundled arms, gained entry through the south and north side gates; by night they burned the Divine Beast Gate and the Zongzhang Observatory, entered the Ministry of the Guards, Hongce climbed the wall and hid in the dragon stable, met the rebels, and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He led several hundred men and, under cover of hauling reed torches and bundled arms, entered through the south and north side gates; by night they burned the Divine Beast Gate and the Zongzhang Observatory and entered the Ministry of the Guards. Hongce climbed the wall and hid in the dragon stable, but the rebels found him and killed him.

sentences.zh: 賊又進燒尚書省及閣道雲龍門，前軍司馬呂僧珍直殿省，帥羽林兵邀擊不能卻。

translations.literal: The rebels advanced further and burned the Secretariat and the covered way to the Cloud Dragon Gate; the former army marshal Lu Sengzhen was on duty in the palace offices and led the Feathered Forest guard to intercept them but could not drive them back.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pressed on and burned the Secretariat and the covered way to the Cloud Dragon Gate. Lu Sengzhen, on duty in the palace offices, led the Feathered Forest guard to intercept them but could not drive them back.

sentences.zh: 上戎服御前殿，謂僧珍曰：「賊夜來是眾少，曉則走矣。」

translations.literal: The Emperor, in military dress, took his seat in the front hall and said to Sengzhen, "The rebels who came by night are few in number; at dawn they will flee."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, in military dress, took his seat in the front hall and said to Sengzhen, "The rebels who came by night are few; at dawn they will scatter."

sentences.zh: 命打五鼓。

translations.literal: He ordered the fifth watch drum struck.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the fifth watch drum struck.

sentences.zh: 賊謂已曉，乃散，官軍捕文明斬於東市，張氏親屬臠食之。

translations.literal: The rebels thought dawn had come and dispersed; the government troops seized Wenming and executed him at the Eastern Market, and Zhang's kinsmen carved up his flesh and ate it.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels thought dawn had come and scattered; government troops seized Wenming and executed him at the Eastern Market, and Zhang's kinsmen carved up his flesh and ate it.

sentences.zh: 帝哭之慟，曰：「痛哉衛尉！

translations.literal: The Emperor wept for him in deep grief and said, "How painful—my Minister of the Guards!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wept bitterly and said, "How painful—my Minister of the Guards!

sentences.zh: 天下事當復與誰論？」

translations.literal: With whom shall I again discuss the affairs of the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: With whom can I discuss the affairs of the realm now?"

sentences.zh: 詔贈車騎將軍，諡曰閔侯。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously awarded him General of Chariots and Cavalry; his posthumous title was Marquis Min.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him General of Chariots and Cavalry with the posthumous title Marquis Min.

sentences.zh: 弘策為人寬厚通率，篤舊故。

translations.literal: Hongce as a man was generous, open, and straightforward, and deeply devoted to old friends.
translations.idiomatic: Hongce was generous, open, and straightforward, and deeply loyal to old friends.

sentences.zh: 及居隆重，不以貴地自高，故人賓客接之如布衣，祿賜皆散之親友。

translations.literal: Even when he held exalted rank he did not set himself above others by his nobility; old friends and guests he received as though they were commoners, and his salary and gifts he distributed among kinsmen and friends.
translations.idiomatic: Even in high office he did not lord his rank over others; he received old friends and guests as though they were commoners, and gave his salary and gifts to kinsmen and friends.

sentences.zh: 及遇害，莫不痛惜焉。

translations.literal: When he met with violence, none failed to grieve for him.
translations.idiomatic: When he was killed, all who knew him grieved.

sentences.zh: 子緬嗣。

translations.literal: His son Mian succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mian succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 緬字元長，年數歲，外祖中山劉仲德異之曰：「此兒非常器，非止為張氏寶，方為海內令名也。」

translations.literal: Mian, styled Yuanchang, was only a few years old when his maternal grandfather Liu Zhongde of Zhongshan, struck by him, said, "This child is no ordinary vessel; he will be not only a treasure to the Zhang clan but a famed name throughout the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Mian, styled Yuanchang, was only a few years old when his maternal grandfather Liu Zhongde of Zhongshan marveled at him and said, "This boy is no ordinary talent; he will be not only the Zhang family's treasure but a name famed throughout the realm."

sentences.zh: 齊永元末兵起，弘策從武帝向都，留緬襄陽，年始十歲，每聞軍有勝負，憂喜形於顏色。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongyuan in Qi, when war broke out, Hongce followed the future Emperor toward the capital and left Mian in Xiangyang; he was just ten years old, and whenever he heard of victory or defeat in the army, worry and joy showed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Qi Yongyuan era, when war broke out, Hongce followed the future Emperor toward the capital and left Mian in Xiangyang. He was only ten, and whenever he heard news of victory or defeat, worry and joy showed plainly on his face.

sentences.zh: 及弘策遇害，緬喪過於禮，武帝每遣喻之。

translations.literal: When Hongce met with violence, Mian observed mourning beyond what the rites required; the Emperor repeatedly sent messengers to console him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongce was killed, Mian mourned beyond what the rites required; the Emperor repeatedly sent messengers to console him.

sentences.zh: 服闋，襲封洮陽縣侯。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he inherited the enfeoffment as Marquis of Taoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he inherited the marquisate of Taoyang.

sentences.zh: 起家秘書郎，出為淮南太守。

translations.literal: He began his career as a Secretary; he went out to serve as Governor of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as a Secretary and was later appointed Governor of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 時年十八，武帝疑其年少，未閑吏事，遣主書封取郡曹文案，見其斷決允愜，甚稱賞之。

translations.literal: He was then eighteen; the Emperor doubted his youth and that he was not yet versed in administrative affairs, and sent a chief clerk to seal and take the commandery office documents; seeing his judgments fair and apt, he greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He was only eighteen; the Emperor doubted whether one so young could yet handle administrative affairs and sent a clerk to seal and fetch the commandery records. Seeing how fair and apt his judgments were, he praised him highly.

sentences.zh: 再遷雲麾外兵參軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to be an outside staff officer on the Cloud Banner staff.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to outside staff officer on the Cloud Banner staff.

sentences.zh: 緬少勤學，自課讀書，手不輟卷。

translations.literal: From youth Mian studied diligently, setting himself lessons in reading, his hand never laying down a scroll.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Mian studied hard, setting himself a daily quota of reading; he never laid down his scroll.

sentences.zh: 有質疑者，隨問便對，略無遺失。

translations.literal: When anyone raised a question, he answered on the spot with scarcely anything missed.
translations.idiomatic: When anyone questioned him, he answered on the spot with scarcely a gap.

sentences.zh: 殿中郎缺，帝謂徐勉曰：「此曹舊用文學，且雁行之首，宜詳擇其人。」

translations.literal: When the post of Palace Attendant fell vacant, the Emperor said to Xu Mian, "This office has traditionally gone to men of letters, and it is the head of the flock—one should choose the man with care."
translations.idiomatic: When the post of Palace Attendant fell vacant, the Emperor said to Xu Mian, "This office has traditionally gone to men of letters, and it leads the flock—choose the man with care."

sentences.zh: 勉舉緬充選。

translations.literal: Mian recommended Mian to fill the selection.
translations.idiomatic: Mian recommended Zhang Mian for the post.

sentences.zh: 頃之，為武陵太守，還拜太子洗馬、中舍人。

translations.literal: Before long he became Governor of Wuling; on his return he was appointed Groom of the Heir Apparent and Palace Attendant of the Center.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he became Governor of Wuling; on his return he was made Groom of the Heir Apparent and Palace Attendant of the Center.

sentences.zh: 緬母劉氏以父沒家貧，葬禮有闕，遂終身不居正室，不隨子入官府。

translations.literal: Mian's mother, the Lady Liu, because her husband had died and the family was poor and the funeral had been deficient, for the rest of her life did not occupy the main chamber and did not follow her son into official residences.
translations.idiomatic: Mian's mother, Lady Liu, because her husband had died poor and the funeral had been inadequate, never occupied the main chamber for the rest of her life and would not enter her son's official residence.

sentences.zh: 緬在郡所得俸祿不敢用，至乃妻子不易衣裳，及還都，並供之母振遺親屬。

translations.literal: Mian in the commandery did not dare use the salary he received; so far did this go that even his wife and children did not change their clothes, and when he returned to the capital he gave it all to his mother to distribute among kinsmen.
translations.idiomatic: In office Mian dared not touch his salary; his wife and children went without new clothes, and when he returned to the capital he gave everything to his mother to distribute among kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 雖累載所蓄，一朝隨盡，緬私室常閼然如貧素者。

translations.literal: Though he had saved for many years, in a single day it was all gone; Mian's private quarters were constantly bare as those of a poor man.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had saved for years, it was all gone in a day; his private quarters were always as bare as a poor man's.

sentences.zh: 累遷豫章內史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Interior Minister of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Interior Minister of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 緬為政任恩惠，不設鉤距，吏人化其德，亦不敢欺。

translations.literal: In government Mian relied on kindness and favor, setting no traps or snares; officials and people were transformed by his virtue and did not dare to deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: In office Mian ruled through kindness and set no traps; officials and commoners alike were moved by his virtue and did not dare deceive him.

sentences.zh: 故老咸云：「數十年未有也」。

translations.literal: The elders all said, "There has been nothing like this in decades."
translations.idiomatic: The elders all said, "There has been nothing like this in decades."

sentences.zh: 後為御史中丞，坐收捕人與外國使鬥，左降黃門，兼領先職，俄復舊任。

translations.literal: Later he became Censor-in-Chief; because men he had arrested fought with foreign envoys, he was demoted to Attendant at the Yellow Gates while retaining his former duties, and soon returned to his old post.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Censor-in-Chief; because men he had arrested fought with foreign envoys, he was demoted to Attendant at the Yellow Gates while keeping his former duties, and soon regained his old post.

sentences.zh: 緬居憲司，推繩無所顧望，號為勁直。

translations.literal: When Mian held the censorate he applied the law without regard for favor and was known as stern and upright.
translations.idiomatic: As censor Mian applied the law without fear or favor and was known for his stern uprightness.

sentences.zh: 武帝乃遣圖其形於台省，以勵當官。

translations.literal: The Emperor then had his likeness painted in the terrace offices to encourage those in office.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had his portrait painted in the terrace offices to encourage those in office.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中，未拜卒，詔便舉哀。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant but died before assuming the post; an edict ordered mourning to be observed at once.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Attendant but died before taking office; an edict ordered immediate mourning.

sentences.zh: 昭明太子亦往臨哭。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Zhaoming also went in person to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Zhaoming also went in person to mourn.

sentences.zh: 緬抄後漢、晉書眾家異同為後漢紀四十卷，晉抄三十卷，又抄江左集未及成，文集五卷。

translations.literal: Mian copied the various discrepancies among accounts of Later Han and Jin into forty juan of Annals of Later Han and thirty juan of Jin Notes; he also copied the Collection of the Eastern Bank, which he did not finish, and five juan of collected writings.
translations.idiomatic: Mian collated differing accounts of Later Han and Jin into forty juan of Annals of Later Han and thirty juan of Jin Notes; he also began a copy of the Collection of the Eastern Bank, which he did not finish, and left five juan of collected writings.

sentences.zh: 緬弟纘。

translations.literal: Mian's younger brother was Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: Mian's younger brother was Zuan.

sentences.zh: 纘字伯緒，出繼從伯弘籍。

translations.literal: Zuan, styled Boxu, was given in succession to his father's cousin Hongji.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan, styled Boxu, was adopted as heir to his father's cousin Hongji.

sentences.zh: 武帝舅也，梁初贈廷尉卿。

translations.literal: He was the Emperor's maternal uncle; at the beginning of Liang he was posthumously made Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was the Emperor's maternal uncle; early in Liang he was posthumously made Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 纘年十一，尚武帝第四女富陽公主，拜駙馬都尉，封利亭侯。

translations.literal: At eleven Zuan married the Emperor's fourth daughter, Princess Fuyang, was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Liting.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven Zuan married the Emperor's fourth daughter, Princess Fuyang, was made Commandant of the Horse Guards, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Liting.

sentences.zh: 召補國子生。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed to fill a vacancy as a student of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and enrolled as a student at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 起家秘書郎，時年十七，身長七尺四寸，眉目疏朗，神采爽發。

translations.literal: He began his career as Secretary Gentleman; at the time he was seventeen, seven feet four inches in height, with clear, refined features and a bright, spirited presence.
translations.idiomatic: He entered official life as a Secretary Gentleman. At seventeen he stood seven feet four inches tall, with refined features and a bright, spirited bearing.

sentences.zh: 武帝異之，嘗曰：「張壯武雲'後八世有逮吾者'，其此子乎。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wu thought him remarkable and once said, "Zhang Zhuangwu said, 'Eight generations hence there will be one who catches up with me'—is it this boy?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was struck by him and once remarked, "Zhang Zhuangwu said, 'Eight generations from now someone will catch up with me'—could it be this boy?"

sentences.zh: 纘好學，兄緬有書萬餘卷，晝夜披讀，殆不輟手。

translations.literal: Zuan loved learning; his elder brother Mian had more than ten thousand scrolls of books, and day and night he spread them open to read, scarcely laying them down.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan loved learning. His elder brother Mian owned more than ten thousand scrolls, and Zuan read them day and night, scarcely setting them aside.

sentences.zh: 秘書郎四員，宋、齊以來，為甲族起家之選，待次入補，其居職例不數十日便遷任。

translations.literal: There were four Secretary Gentlemen; since the Song and Qi dynasties this had been the office chosen for great clans at the start of their careers—one waited his turn to fill a post, and those who held the office typically transferred within ten days or so.
translations.idiomatic: There were four Secretary Gentlemen. Since Song and Qi times the post had been the usual starting place for eminent clans: one waited in queue for a vacancy, and incumbents typically moved on within ten days.

sentences.zh: 纘固求不徙，欲遍觀閣內書籍。

translations.literal: Zuan firmly requested not to be transferred, wishing to read through all the books in the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan firmly asked not to be moved, wanting to read every book in the archive.

sentences.zh: 嘗執四部書目曰：「若讀此畢，可言優仕矣。」

translations.literal: Once, holding the catalogue of the four departments of books, he said, "If I finish reading this, one may speak of eminent appointment."
translations.idiomatic: Once, holding the catalogue of the four library divisions, he said, "When I have finished this, I may call myself fit for high office."

sentences.zh: 如此三載，方遷太子舍人，轉洗馬，中舍人，並掌管記。

translations.literal: After three years in this way he was finally promoted to Attendant of the Heir Apparent, then transferred to Groom, then Central Attendant-in-Ordinary—all posts managing records.
translations.idiomatic: After three years of this he was promoted to Attendant of the Heir Apparent, then Groom, then Central Attendant-in-Ordinary, all posts concerned with keeping the records.

sentences.zh: 纘與琅邪王錫齊名。

translations.literal: Zuan and Wang Xi of Langya were equally famed.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan and Wang Xi of Langya were equally renowned.

sentences.zh: 普通初，魏使彭城人劉善明通和，求識纘與錫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Puzhou era, Wei sent Liu Shanming of Pengcheng to establish peaceful relations and asked to meet Zuan and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Puzhou reign, Wei sent Liu Shanming of Pengcheng to negotiate peace and asked to meet Zuan and Xi.

sentences.zh: 纘時年二十三，善明見而嗟服。

translations.literal: Zuan was then twenty-three; when Shanming saw him he sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan was twenty-three at the time; Shanming met him and sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書吏部郎，俄而長兼侍中，時人以為早達。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Director of the Secretariat's Department of Personnel, and soon after held the post of Attendant-in-Ordinary on a long-term concurrent basis; people of the time regarded this as early advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Director of the Department of Personnel and soon held a long-term concurrent appointment as Attendant-in-Ordinary; contemporaries considered this precocious promotion.

sentences.zh: 河東裴子野曰：「張吏部有喉唇之任，已恨其晚矣。」

translations.literal: Pei Ziye of Hedong said, "Director Zhang has the charge of the state's throat and lips—already one regrets that it came late."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ziye of Hedong remarked, "Director Zhang holds the nation's voice in his hands—even now we regret the appointment came so late."

sentences.zh: 子野性曠達，自雲年出三十不復詣人。

translations.literal: Ziye was by nature broad and unconstrained; he himself said that after passing thirty he would visit no one again.
translations.idiomatic: Ziye was by nature free-spirited and broad-minded; he declared that after thirty he would pay calls on no one.

sentences.zh: 初未與纘遇，便虛相推重，因為忘年之交。

translations.literal: Before he had even met Zuan he already esteemed him without cause, and thus they became friends across the age gap.
translations.idiomatic: Before he had even met Zuan he already held him in high regard, and they became friends despite the difference in age.

sentences.zh: 大通中，為吳興太守，居郡省煩苛，務清靜，人吏便之。

translations.literal: In the Datong era he was Prefect of Wu-xing; in the commandery he reduced troublesome severity and sought tranquillity and quiet; officials and the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: During Datong he served as Prefect of Wu-xing, cutting red tape and favoring quiet governance; officials and commoners alike found his rule a relief.

sentences.zh: 大同二年，徵為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong he was summoned as Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Datong he was summoned to serve as Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後門寒素一介者，皆見引拔，不為貴門屈意，人士翕然稱之。

translations.literal: Those from humble houses who were poor but upright were all introduced and promoted; he would not bend his will to noble clans, and men of letters unanimously praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted men from poor but upright backgrounds and would not defer to great families; the literati praised him in unison.

sentences.zh: 負其才氣，無所與讓。

translations.literal: He relied on his talent and spirit and yielded to no one.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his talent and spirit, he yielded to no one.

sentences.zh: 定襄侯祗無學術，頗有文性，與兄衡山侯恭俱為皇太子愛賞。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Dingxiang, Zhi, had no learning but possessed some literary talent; with his elder brother the Marquis of Hengshan, Gong, both were loved and admired by the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Dingxiang, Zhi, had little learning but some literary flair; he and his elder brother the Marquis of Hengshan, Gong, were both favorites of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 時纘從兄謐、聿並不學問，性又凡愚。

translations.literal: At the time Zuan's cousins Mi and Lü were both without learning and by nature coarse and foolish.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zuan's cousins Mi and Lü were unlearned and by nature dull and foolish.

sentences.zh: 恭、祗嘗預東宮盛集，太子戲纘曰：「丈人謐、聿皆何在？」

translations.literal: Gong and Zhi once attended a grand gathering in the Eastern Palace; the Crown Prince joked to Zuan, "Where are your uncles Mi and Lü?"
translations.idiomatic: Gong and Zhi once attended a grand gathering in the Eastern Palace. The Crown Prince teased Zuan: "Where are your uncles Mi and Lü?"

sentences.zh: 纘從容曰：「纘有謐、聿，亦殿下之衡、定。」

translations.literal: Zuan calmly replied, "Zuan has Mi and Lü—also Your Highness's Heng and Ding."
translations.idiomatic: Zuan replied calmly, "I have Mi and Lü—just as Your Highness has Heng and Ding."

sentences.zh: 太子色慚。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince's face turned ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince flushed with embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 或云纘從兄聿及弼愚短，湘東王在坐，問纘曰：「丈人二從聿、弼藝業何如？」

translations.literal: Some say Zuan's cousins Lü and Bi were stupid and short; the Prince of Xiangdong was present and asked Zuan, "How are the arts and achievements of your two cousins Lü and Bi?"
translations.idiomatic: According to another account, Zuan's cousins Lü and Bi were dull and slight of stature. The Prince of Xiangdong was present and asked Zuan, "How do your cousins Lü and Bi fare in learning and accomplishment?"

sentences.zh: 纘曰：「下官從弟雖並無多，猶賢殿下之有衡、定。」

translations.literal: Zuan said, "My humble cousins, though they have not much between them, are still preferable to Your Highness having Heng and Ding."
translations.idiomatic: Zuan said, "My cousins may not amount to much, but they are still better than Your Highness having Heng and Ding."

sentences.zh: 舉坐愕然，其忤物如此。

translations.literal: The whole assembly was startled—such was his way of offending people.
translations.idiomatic: The whole company was stunned—such was his manner of giving offense.

sentences.zh: 五年，武帝詔曰：「纘外氏英華，朝中領袖，司空已後，名冠范陽。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Emperor Wu's edict said, "Zuan, of the maternal clan's brilliance, a leader in court; after the Minister of Works, his name topped Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Emperor Wu issued an edict: "Zuan, flower of the maternal clan and leader at court; since the Minister of Works, his name has stood first in Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 可尚書僕射。」

translations.literal: He may be appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 纘本寒門，以外戚顯重，高自擬倫，而詔有「司空范陽。」

translations.literal: Zuan was originally from a humble house; through maternal relatives he had become prominent and set himself high among peers, yet the edict had the words "Minister of Works, Fanyang."
translations.idiomatic: Zuan came from a humble family and had risen through his ties to the imperial consort clan, holding himself in high esteem; yet the edict spoke of "the Minister of Works of Fanyang."

sentences.zh: 之言，深用為狹。

translations.literal: He deeply took this as narrow-minded and insulting.
translations.idiomatic: He took this deeply as a slight.

sentences.zh: 以朱異草詔，與異不平。

translations.literal: Because Zhu Yi had drafted the edict, he was at odds with Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Zhu Yi had drafted the edict, he bore a grudge against Yi.

sentences.zh: 初，纘與參掌何敬容意趣不協，敬容居權軸，賓客輻湊，有過詣纘，纘輒距不前，曰：「吾不能對何敬容殘客。」

translations.literal: Earlier Zuan and He Jingrong, who shared in administration, were not in accord; Jingrong held the pivot of power and guests thronged about him; if any who had faults came to visit Zuan, Zuan would refuse to advance and say, "I cannot face He Jingrong's remnant guests."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zuan had clashed with He Jingrong, his fellow administrator. Jingrong held the levers of power and his hall was always crowded. When disgraced clients of Jingrong came to call on Zuan, he would turn them away, saying, "I will not sit with He Jingrong's cast-off guests."

sentences.zh: 及是遷，為讓表曰：「自出守股肱，入居衡尺，可以仰首伸眉，論列是非者矣。

translations.literal: Upon this transfer he submitted a letter of declination saying, "Since leaving to guard the realm as a limb and entering to occupy the measuring rod, one could raise one's head, stretch one's brows, and discuss right and wrong—
translations.idiomatic: On this promotion he submitted a letter declining the post: "From governing a province to holding the central scales, one might at last raise one's head and speak plainly about right and wrong—

sentences.zh: 而寸衿所滯，近蔽耳目，深淺清濁，豈有能預。

translations.literal: yet the inch of collar that stagnates recently blinds ears and eyes—shallow and deep, clear and muddy—how can one preside over them?
translations.idiomatic: yet petty entanglements now blind me at close range; how can I judge what is shallow or deep, clear or foul?

sentences.zh: 加以矯心飾貌，酷非所閑，不喜俗人，與之共事。」

translations.literal: Adding to that, feigning the heart and decorating the appearance is utterly not what I am versed in; I do not like vulgar people or working with them."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, dissembling and posturing are skills I utterly lack, and I have no taste for working alongside vulgar men."

sentences.zh: 此言以指敬容也。

translations.literal: These words were meant to point at Jingrong.
translations.idiomatic: These words were aimed at Jingrong.

sentences.zh: 在職議南郊禦乘素輦，適古今之衷。

translations.literal: While in office he proposed that for the southern suburb the emperor should ride the plain palanquin—fitting the mean of past and present.
translations.idiomatic: In office he argued that at the southern suburban rites the emperor should ride an unadorned carriage, a compromise suited to ancient and modern practice.

sentences.zh: 又議印綬官若備朝服，宜並著綬。

translations.literal: He also proposed that officials with seals and cords, if wearing full court dress, should also wear the cord.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed that officials bearing seals and cords should wear the cord whenever they wore full court dress.

sentences.zh: 時並施行。

translations.literal: At the time both were put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Both proposals were adopted at the time.

sentences.zh: 改為湘州刺史，述職經塗，作南征賦。

translations.literal: He was changed to Inspector of Xiangzhou; on the journey to take up his post he composed the "Rhapsody on the Southern Expedition."
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Inspector of Xiangzhou and, en route to his post, wrote the Rhapsody on the Southern Expedition.

sentences.zh: 初，吳興吳規頗有才學，邵陵王綸引為賓客，深相禮遇。

translations.literal: Earlier Wu Gui of Wu-xing was quite learned; Prince Shao-ling Lun employed him as a retainer and greatly honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wu Gui of Wu-xing was a man of considerable learning. Prince Shao-ling Lun took him as a client and treated him with great respect.

sentences.zh: 及綸作牧郢蕃，規隨從江夏。

translations.literal: When Lun became prefect of Ye and Fan, Gui followed him to Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: When Lun was made prefect of Ye and Fan, Gui accompanied him to Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 遇纘出之湘鎮，路經郢服，綸餞之南浦。

translations.literal: It happened that Zuan was departing for the Xiang commandery; his route passed through Ye territory, and Lun entertained him at Nanpu.
translations.idiomatic: When Zuan set out for the Xiang region his route passed through Ye, and Lun gave him a farewell feast at Nanpu.

sentences.zh: 纘見規在坐，意不能平，忽舉杯曰：「吳規，此酒慶汝得陪今宴。」

translations.literal: Zuan saw Gui in the seats and could not be at peace; suddenly raising his cup he said, "Wu Gui—this cup celebrates your being able to join today's feast."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Gui among the guests, Zuan could not contain his resentment. He suddenly raised his cup and said, "Wu Gui—this drink celebrates your good fortune in joining today's banquet."

sentences.zh: 規尋起還，其子翁孺見父不悅，問而知之，翁孺因氣結，爾夜便卒。

translations.literal: Gui soon rose and left; his son Wengru, seeing his father displeased, asked and learned why; Wengru then from anger knotted up, and that very night died.
translations.idiomatic: Gui rose at once and withdrew. His son Wengru, seeing his father's distress, asked and learned the cause; that night Wengru died of choked rage.

sentences.zh: 規恨纘慟兒，憤哭兼至，信次之間又致殞。

translations.literal: Gui hated Zuan for his grieving son; weeping and fury together reached the extreme; within the interval of sending word he also died.
translations.idiomatic: Gui blamed Zuan for his son's death and gave way to grief and fury; before the messenger could return, he too was dead.

sentences.zh: 規妻深痛夫、子，翌日又亡。

translations.literal: Gui's wife deeply grieved husband and son; the next day she too died.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's wife, stricken by the loss of husband and son, died the following day.

sentences.zh: 時人謂張纘一杯酒殺吳氏三人，其輕傲皆此類也。

translations.literal: Men of the time said Zhang Zuan killed the three of the Wu family with one cup of wine—such were all his insults.
translations.idiomatic: People said Zhang Zuan had killed three members of the Wu family with a single cup of wine—such was the measure of his arrogance.

sentences.zh: 至州務公平，遣十郡慰勞，解放老疾吏役，及關市戍邏、先所防人，一皆省並，州界零陵、衡陽等郡有莫徭蠻者，依山險為居，曆政不賓服，因此向化。

translations.literal: Arriving at the province he pursued fairness in affairs; sent envoys to ten commanderies to offer consolation; released old and sick clerks and corvée; all frontier guards at markets and passes and persons previously detained were reduced and merged; in the province Lingling, Hengyang, and other commanderies had Mo-yao barbarians who lived in mountainous defiles—through successive administrations they had not submitted, and thereby turned toward civilization.
translations.idiomatic: In the province he governed fairly, sent envoys to ten commanderies to offer comfort, released aged and infirm clerks from service, and cut frontier guards, market posts, and previously detained persons. In Lingling, Hengyang, and other commanderies Mo-yao tribes had long lived in the hills and refused submission; under his rule they came to accept imperial authority.

sentences.zh: 益陽縣人作田二頃，皆異畝同穎。

translations.literal: A man of Yiyang district worked two qing of fields—all different stalks with the same ears.
translations.idiomatic: In Yiyang district a farmer's two qing of fields bore different stalks but identical ears of grain.

sentences.zh: 在政四年，流人自歸，戶口增十餘萬，州境大寧。

translations.literal: In government four years, wandering people returned of themselves; households increased by more than a hundred thousand; the province's borders were greatly peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: After four years in office displaced people returned on their own; the population grew by more than a hundred thousand households; and the province knew great tranquillity.

sentences.zh: 晚頗好積聚，多寫圖書數萬卷，有油二百斛，米四千石，佗物稱是。

translations.literal: Later he became quite fond of amassing goods; he copied many books numbering tens of thousands of scrolls, had two hundred hu of oil, four thousand shi of rice, and other goods in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he grew fond of hoarding wealth. He copied tens of thousands of scrolls of books and amassed two hundred hu of oil, four thousand shi of rice, and comparable stores of other goods.

sentences.zh: 太清二年，徙授領軍，俄改雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiqing he was transferred and appointed Commander of the Guards, and soon after changed to Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiqing he was transferred to Commander of the Guards, then soon reassigned as Inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 初聞邵陵王綸當代己為湘州，其後更用河東王譽。

translations.literal: At first he heard Prince Shao-ling Lun would replace him in Xiangzhou, but afterward Prince of Hedong Yu was used instead.
translations.idiomatic: At first he heard that Prince Shao-ling Lun would succeed him in Xiangzhou, but in the end Prince of Hedong Yu was appointed.

sentences.zh: 纘素輕少王，州府候迎及資待甚薄。

translations.literal: Zuan had always looked down on the young prince; the prefecture and mansion's reception and supplies were very meager.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan had always despised the young prince, and the prefectural offices offered him a thin welcome and scant provisions.

sentences.zh: 譽深銜之。

translations.literal: Yu deeply resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Yu bore a deep grudge.

sentences.zh: 及至州，譽遂托疾不見纘，仍檢括州府庶事，留纘不遣。

translations.literal: When he arrived at the province, Yu feigned illness and would not see Zuan, still inspected and checked the prefecture's affairs, and kept Zuan from departing.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu reached the province he pleaded illness and refused to see Zuan, took control of prefectural affairs, and detained Zuan from leaving.

sentences.zh: 會聞侯景寇建鄴，譽當下援。

translations.literal: It happened that they heard Hou Jing was raiding Jianye; Yu was to go down in aid.
translations.idiomatic: Word came that Hou Jing was attacking Jianye, and Yu was to march to the capital's relief.

sentences.zh: 湘東王時鎮江陵，與纘有舊，纘將因之以斃譽兄弟。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiangdong was then stationed at Jiangling and had old ties with Zuan; Zuan intended to rely on him to destroy Yu and his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiangdong was then at Jiangling and had long been close to Zuan; Zuan planned to use him to destroy Yu and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 時湘東王與譽及信州刺史桂陽王慥各率所領入援台，下硤至江津，譽次江口，湘東王屆郢州之武城。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Xiangdong with Yu and the Inspector of Xinzhou, the Prince of Guiyang Chao, each led their forces to aid the capital, descending the gorge to the ford at the river; Yu halted at the river mouth; the Prince of Xiangdong reached Wucheng in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiangdong, Yu, and the Prince of Guiyang Chao, Inspector of Xinzhou, each led their troops to relieve the capital, descending the gorge to the river crossing. Yu encamped at the river mouth while the Prince of Xiangdong reached Wucheng in Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 屬侯景已請和，武帝詔罷援軍。

translations.literal: Just then Hou Jing had requested peace; Emperor Wu ordered the relief army disbanded.
translations.idiomatic: By then Hou Jing had sued for peace, and Emperor Wu ordered the relief forces withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 譽自江口將旋湘鎮，欲待湘東至，謁督府，方還州。

translations.literal: Yu from the river mouth was about to turn back to the Xiang commandery, wishing to wait until the Prince of Xiangdong arrived, pay respects at the supervisory headquarters, then return to his province.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was about to withdraw from the river mouth to Xiangzhou, intending to wait for the Prince of Xiangdong, pay his respects at headquarters, and then return home.

sentences.zh: 纘乃貽湘東書曰：「河東戴檣上水，欲襲江陵；

translations.literal: Zuan then sent a letter to the Prince of Xiangdong saying, "The Prince of Hedong, with banners on the stream going upstream, intends to attack Jiangling;
translations.idiomatic: Zuan then wrote to the Prince of Xiangdong: "The Prince of Hedong is sailing upstream under arms and intends to strike Jiangling;

sentences.zh: 岳陽在雍，共謀不逞。」

translations.literal: Yueyang is at Yong—they plot together and will not desist."
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Yueyang at Yong is in league with him in a treasonous plot."

sentences.zh: 江陵游軍主朱榮又遣使報云：「桂陽住此欲應譽、察。」

translations.literal: The roaming-army commander Zhu Rong at Jiangling also sent a messenger reporting, "Guiyang is staying here intending to respond to Yu and Cha."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Rong, commander of the roaming forces at Jiangling, also sent word: "The Prince of Guiyang is lingering here, ready to join Yu and Cha."

sentences.zh: 湘東信之，乃鑿船沈米，斬纜而歸。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiangdong believed it; then he scuttled boats, sank rice, cut cables, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiangdong believed him, scuttled his boats, dumped his grain, cut his moorings, and hurried back.

sentences.zh: 至江陵收慥殺之。

translations.literal: Arriving at Jiangling he seized and killed Chao.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Jiangling he seized Chao and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 荊、湘因構嫌隙。

translations.literal: Jing and Xiang thereby built mutual suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Thus mutual enmity arose between Jing and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 纘尋棄其部曲，攜其二女，單舸赴江陵。

translations.literal: Zuan soon abandoned his troops, taking his two daughters in a single boat to rush to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan soon abandoned his troops, took his two daughters in a lone boat, and fled to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 湘東遣使責讓譽，索纘部下，仍遣纘向雍州。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiangdong sent an envoy to rebuke Yu, demanded Zuan's subordinates, and still sent Zuan toward Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiangdong sent an envoy to rebuke Yu, demanded Zuan's troops, and dispatched Zuan on to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 前刺史岳陽王察推遷未去鎮，但以城西白馬寺處之。

translations.literal: The former inspector the Prince of Yueyang Cha had been promoted but not yet left the post; he merely lodged Zuan at White Horse Temple west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: The former inspector, the Prince of Yueyang Cha, had been promoted but had not yet vacated his post; he lodged Zuan at White Horse Temple west of the city.

sentences.zh: 會聞賊陷台城，察因不受代。

translations.literal: It happened that they heard the rebels had taken Taicheng; Cha therefore did not accept succession.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that the rebels had taken Taicheng, Cha refused to yield his post.

sentences.zh: 州助防杜岸紿纘曰：「觀岳陽不容使君，使君素得物情，若走入西山義舉，事無不濟。」

translations.literal: The provincial assistant for defense Du An deceived Zuan, saying, "Seeing that Yueyang will not tolerate you, sir—you have always won people's hearts; if you flee into the western hills to raise a righteous campaign, nothing will fail."
translations.idiomatic: Du An, assistant for defense, deceived Zuan: "The Prince of Yueyang will not tolerate you, yet you have always had the people's sympathy. If you flee into the western hills and raise a righteous force, you cannot fail."

sentences.zh: 纘以為然。

translations.literal: Zuan thought it so.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan believed him.

sentences.zh: 因與岸兄弟盟，乃要雍州人席引等於西山聚眾。

translations.literal: He then allied with An's brothers, and summoned people of Yongzhou like Xi Yin at the western hills to gather a crowd.
translations.idiomatic: He allied with An and his brothers and summoned men of Yongzhou such as Xi Yin to gather a force in the western hills.

sentences.zh: 乃服婦人衣，乘青布輿，與親信十餘人奔引等。

translations.literal: He then donned women's clothes, rode a plain cloth palanquin, and with more than ten close followers fled to Yin and the others.
translations.idiomatic: He dressed as a woman, rode in a plain cloth carriage, and with a dozen trusted followers fled to join Yin and his band.

sentences.zh: 杜岸馳告察，察令中兵參軍尹正等追討。

translations.literal: Du An rode in haste to inform Cha; Cha ordered the Central Army Army Supervisor Yin Zheng and others to pursue and attack.
translations.idiomatic: Du An galloped to inform Cha, who ordered Yin Zheng of the Central Army staff and others to pursue and capture him.

sentences.zh: 纘以為赴期，大喜，及至並禽之。

translations.literal: Zuan thought he had reached the appointed time and was greatly pleased; when he arrived they were all captured together.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan thought he had reached his allies and rejoiced—but on arrival he and his party were seized.

sentences.zh: 纘懼不免，請為沙門，名法緒。

translations.literal: Zuan, fearing he could not escape, requested to become a monk, taking the name Fazuo.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing execution, Zuan asked to become a monk and took the religious name Fazuo.

sentences.zh: 察襲江陵，常載纘隨後，逼使為檄，固辭以疾。

translations.literal: When Cha attacked Jiangling he always carried Zuan behind him, forcing him to draft proclamations; he firmly refused citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Cha marched on Jiangling he kept Zuan with his train and pressed him to write proclamations; Zuan steadfastly pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 及軍退敗，行至湕水南，防守纘者慮追兵至，遂害之，棄屍而去。

translations.literal: When the army retreated in defeat, as they reached the south of the Han River, those guarding Zuan, fearing pursuing troops would arrive, then killed him and cast away the corpse.
translations.idiomatic: When the army was routed and they reached the south bank of the Han, his guards, fearing pursuit, killed him and abandoned his body.

sentences.zh: 元帝承制，贈開府儀同三司，諡簡憲公。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan, acting on imperial authority, posthumously awarded him Grand Master of Splendid State with the same ceremonial rank as the Three Excellencies and gave him the posthumous title Duke Jianxian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan, exercising imperial authority, posthumously made him Grand Master of Splendid State with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies and titled him Duke Jianxian.

sentences.zh: 元帝少時，纘便推誠委結，及帝即位，追思之，嘗為詩序云：「簡憲之為人也，不事王侯，負才任氣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan was young, Zuan had already entrusted himself to him sincerely; when the Emperor took the throne he recalled this and once wrote in a preface to a poem, "Jianxian as a man did not serve kings and marquises; he bore his talent and undertook his spirit.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Emperor Yuan had won Zuan's wholehearted loyalty; after his accession he looked back on this and once wrote in a preface to a poem: "Duke Jianxian was a man who would not serve kings and lords; he carried his talent and his pride.

sentences.zh: 見余則申旦達夕，不能已已。

translations.literal: Seeing me he would talk from dawn till dusk, unable to stop.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw me he would talk from dawn till dusk and could not have enough of my company.

sentences.zh: 懷夫人之德，何日忘之。」

translations.literal: I cherish the virtue of such a man—how could I forget it in a day?"
translations.idiomatic: I cherish such a man's goodness—how could I ever forget it?"

sentences.zh: 纘著鴻寶一百卷，文集二十卷。

translations.literal: Zuan authored Hongbao in one hundred scrolls and a collection of writings in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan wrote the Hongbao in one hundred scrolls and a collection of writings in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 初，纘之往雍州，資產悉留江陵。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zuan went to Yongzhou, his property was entirely left at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: When Zuan first went to Yongzhou he left all his property at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 性既貪婪，南中貲賄填積。

translations.literal: His nature being greedy, southern goods and bribes piled up.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy by nature, he had amassed a fortune in southern goods and bribes.

sentences.zh: 及死，湘東王皆使收之，書二萬卷並摙還齋，珍寶財物悉付庫，以粽蜜之屬還其家。

translations.literal: After his death the Prince of Xiangdong had everything collected; twenty thousand scrolls of books were bundled and returned to the studio; treasures and valuables were all sent to the storehouse; rice-dumplings, honey, and the like were returned to his family.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the Prince of Xiangdong seized it all: twenty thousand scrolls of books were bundled back to the palace library, jewels and goods sent to the treasury, and only rice dumplings, honey, and the like were returned to his family.

sentences.zh: 次子希字子顏，早知名，尚簡文第九女海鹽公主。

translations.literal: His second son Xi, styled Ziyan, was early known; he married the Ninth Daughter of Emperor Jianwen, Princess Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Xi, styled Ziyan, won early renown and married the Ninth Daughter of Emperor Jianwen, Princess Haiyan.

sentences.zh: 承聖初，位侍中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chengsheng he reached the post of Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chengsheng era he rose to Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 纘弟綰。

translations.literal: Zuan's younger brother Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's younger brother was Chao.

sentences.zh: 綰字孝卿，少與兄纘齊名。

translations.literal: Chao, styled Xiaqing, from youth was as famous as his elder brother Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chao, styled Xiaqing, had been as famous as his elder brother Zuan since youth.

sentences.zh: 湘東王繹嘗策之百事，綰對闕其六，號為百六公。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiangdong Xiao Yi once tested him on a hundred matters; Chao answered lacking six—he was called Duke of the Hundred-Six.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiangdong Xiao Yi once quizzed him on a hundred topics; Chao failed six and was nicknamed Duke of the Hundred-Six.

sentences.zh: 位員外散騎常侍、中軍宣城王長史。

translations.literal: He reached the posts of Supernumerary Regular Attendant and Chief Clerk to the Prince of Xuancheng of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Supernumerary Regular Attendant and Chief Clerk to the Prince of Xuancheng under the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 武帝遣其弟中書舍人絢宣旨曰：「為國之急，唯在執憲直繩，用人之本，不限升降。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu sent his younger brother the Secretariat Attendant-in-Ordinary Xuan to proclaim the intent, saying, "The urgent matter for the state lies only in holding the law with a straight cord; the root of employing men is not limited to promotion or demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu sent Chao's younger brother Xuan, Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Secretariat, to announce the imperial will: "A state's urgent need is to enforce the law impartially; the foundation of appointing men is not whether they rise or fall in rank.

sentences.zh: 晉、宋時，周閔、蔡廓兼以侍中為之，卿勿疑是左遷。」

translations.literal: In Jin and Song times Zhou Min and Cai Kuo both held the post concurrently with Attendant-in-Ordinary—you, sir, must not suspect this is a lateral transfer."
translations.idiomatic: In Jin and Song times Zhou Min and Cai Kuo both held the censorate while serving as Attendant-in-Ordinary—do not take this as a demotion."

sentences.zh: 時宣城王府望重，故有此旨焉。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Xuancheng's house was weighty in prestige, hence this decree.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xuancheng's household was then so eminent that this special reassurance was given.

sentences.zh: 大同四年元日，舊制僕射中丞坐位東西相當，時綰兄纘為僕射，及百司就列，兄弟並導騶分趨兩陛，前代未有，時人榮之。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the fourth year of Datong, by old regulation the seats of the Vice Grand Minister and the Censor-in-Chief were east and west facing each other equally; at that time Wan's elder brother Huan held the post of Vice Grand Minister, and when the hundred offices took their places, the brothers both led their escorts and split to hurry to the two flights of steps—unprecedented in former ages, and people of the time took pride in it.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day in the fourth year of Datong, custom placed the Vice Grand Minister and the Censor-in-Chief in seats of equal rank, east and west. Wan's elder brother Huan was then Vice Grand Minister; when the bureaucracy assembled for court, both brothers rode at the head of their escorts and marched up opposite stairways—a spectacle never seen before, and one their contemporaries counted a glory.

sentences.zh: 出為豫章內史，在郡述制旨禮記正言義，四姓衣冠士子聽者常數百人。

translations.literal: He went out as Intendant of Yuzhang; in the commandery he expounded the meaning of the Imperially Commissioned Correct Meaning of the Record of Rites; gentry of the four surnames and capped-and-robed scholars who listened often numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Intendant of Yuzhang, he lectured in the prefecture on the court-sponsored Correct Meaning of the Record of Rites, drawing several hundred listeners from the leading families and the scholar-gentry.

sentences.zh: 八年，安成人劉敬宮挾祅道，遂聚黨攻郡，進寇豫章，刺史湘東王遣司馬王僧辯討賊，受綰節度。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Liu Jinggong of Ancheng, relying on heterodox teachings, then gathered a faction to attack the commandery and advanced to raid Yuzhang; the Inspector, the Prince of Xiangdong, sent the Marshal Wang Senbian to pacify the bandits, subject to Wan's command.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Liu Jinggong of Ancheng led a cult following in revolt against the commandery and pushed into Yuzhang. The Prince of Xiangdong, as regional inspector, sent Marshal Wang Senbian against the rebels under Wan's overall command.

sentences.zh: 旬月間，賊党悉平。

translations.literal: Within a month and a half, the rebel faction was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month and a half the rebels were wholly suppressed.

sentences.zh: 十年，復為御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he again became Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was again appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 綰再為憲司，彈糾無所回避，豪右憚之。

translations.literal: Wan again held the office of censor; impeaching and investigating, he avoided nothing; powerful families feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Serving a second term as chief censor, he censured wrongdoing without flinching, and the great houses learned to fear him.

sentences.zh: 時城西開士林館聚學者，綰與右衛朱異、太府卿賀琛遞述制旨禮記中庸義。

translations.literal: At that time west of the city the Forest of Scholars Hall was opened to gather scholars; Wan together with the Right Guard Zhu Yi and the Grand Steward He Chen took turns expounding the meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean from the Imperially Commissioned Record of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: A Forest of Scholars academy opened west of the capital, and Wan, Zhu Yi of the Right Guard, and He Chen, Grand Steward of the Court Treasury, alternated in lecturing on the Mean from the imperial commentary on the Record of Rites.

sentences.zh: 太清三年，為吏部尚書，宮城陷，奔江陵，位尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiqing, he became Minister of the Civil Office; the palace city fell; he fled to Jiangling and took the post of Vice Minister of the Right of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiqing he was made Minister of the Civil Office; when the capital fell he fled to Jiangling and was appointed Vice Minister of the Right of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 魏克江陵，朝士皆俘入關，綰以疾免，卒於江陵。

translations.literal: When Wei took Jiangling, court scholars were all captured and taken into the pass; Wan was excused because of illness and died at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei captured Jiangling, the court elite were marched captive into the north; Wan, spared because of illness, died in Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 次子交，字少游，尚簡文第十一女定陽公主。

translations.literal: His second son Jiao, style name Shaoyou, married the eleventh daughter of Emperor Jianwen, the Princess of Dingyang.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Jiao (Shaoyou) married Emperor Jianwen's eleventh daughter, Princess Dingyang.

sentences.zh: 承聖二年，官至秘書丞，掌東宮管記。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chengsheng, his office reached Secretary Director, in charge of the Eastern Palace Secretariat records.
translations.idiomatic: By the second year of Chengsheng he had risen to Secretary Director and oversaw the Eastern Palace secretarial records.

sentences.zh: 庾域字司大，新野人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Yu, style name Sida, was a man of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yu (Sida) was from Xinye.

sentences.zh: 少沈靜，有名鄉曲。

translations.literal: In youth he was quiet and composed, with a name in his village and lanes.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was calm and reserved and already had a reputation in his home district.

sentences.zh: 梁文帝為郢州，辟為主簿，歎美其才，曰：「荊南杞梓，其在斯乎。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Liang was at Yingzhou, he summoned him as Chief Clerk, sighed in praise of his talent, and said: "The catalpa and cedar south of Jing—are they here?"
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Wen held Yingzhou, he recruited Yuan as chief clerk, marveled at his talent, and said, "The finest timber of southern Jing—might it be standing here?"

sentences.zh: 加以恩禮。

translations.literal: He moreover bestowed favor and courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: He treated him with especial favor and respect.

sentences.zh: 長沙宣武王為梁州，以為錄事參軍，帶華陽太守。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Changsha, Xuanwu, was at Liangzhou, he made him Recording Secretary Advisor, concurrently Huayang Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xuanwu of Changsha governed Liangzhou, he appointed Yuan recording secretary and acting administrator of Huayang.

sentences.zh: 時魏軍攻圍南鄭，州有空倉數十所，域手自封題，指示將士曰：「此中粟皆滿，足支二年。

translations.literal: At the time Wei troops besieged Nanzheng; the province had several dozen empty granaries; Yu personally sealed and labeled them, pointed them out to officers and soldiers, and said: "The grain in these is all full, enough to support for two years.
translations.idiomatic: While Wei forces besieged Nanzheng, the province held dozens of empty granaries. Yu personally sealed each one and assured the troops, "These are stocked full—grain enough for two years.

sentences.zh: 但努力堅守。」

translations.literal: Only strive hard to hold firm."
translations.idiomatic: Hold the line with all your strength."

sentences.zh: 眾心以安。

translations.literal: The hearts of the masses were thereby calmed.
translations.idiomatic: The army's spirit steadied at once.

sentences.zh: 軍退，以功拜羽林監。

translations.literal: When the army withdrew, by merit he was appointed Supervisor of the Forest of Feathers.
translations.idiomatic: After the enemy withdrew he was rewarded with appointment as Supervisor of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 及長沙王為益州，域隨為懷甯太守。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Changsha was at Yizhou, Yu followed as Huaining Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Changsha took Yizhou, Yuan followed him as administrator of Huaining.

sentences.zh: 罷任還家，妻子猶事井臼，而域所衣大布，餘奉專充供養。

translations.literal: Leaving office and returning home, his wife and children still tended the mortar and pestle, while Yu wore coarse hemp cloth; the remainder of his salary was devoted entirely to supporting his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Back home after his term, his wife and children still ground grain at the mortar while he wore plain homespun; whatever remained of his stipend went entirely to his parents' support.

sentences.zh: 母好鶴唳，域在位營求，孜孜不怠，一旦雙鶴來下，論者以為孝感所致。

translations.literal: His mother loved the cry of cranes; Yu while in office sought to provide them, diligent and unwearying; one day a pair of cranes came down; commentators took it as brought about by filial feeling moving heaven.
translations.idiomatic: His mother delighted in the cry of cranes. While in office Yuan labored to satisfy her wish; one day a pair of cranes descended, and many read it as heaven's answer to his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 永元初，南康王板西中郎諮議參軍，母憂去職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongyuan, the Prince of Nankang appointed him Western Central Commander Advisory Staff Member; on his mother's death he left office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongyuan era the Prince of Nankang named him advisory staff officer of the Western Central Commander; he resigned upon his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝舉兵，起為甯朔將軍，領行選。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang raised troops, he was summoned as General Pacifying the North and supervised provisional selections.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took up arms, Yuan was recalled as General Pacifying the North with charge of provisional personnel selection.

sentences.zh: 武帝東下，師次楊口，和帝遣御史中丞宗夬勞軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu marched east; the army halted at Yangkou; Emperor He sent Censor-in-Chief Zong Que to comfort the troops.
translations.idiomatic: As Emperor Wu drove east his army encamped at Yangkou, and Emperor He sent Censor-in-Chief Zong Que to reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 域乃諷夬曰：「黃鉞未加，非所以總率侯伯。」

translations.literal: Yu then obliquely said to Que: "The yellow battle-axe has not yet been conferred; this is not the way to command the feudal lords."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan obliquely told Que, "Without the yellow battle-axe he cannot truly command the feudal lords."

sentences.zh: 夬反，西台即授武帝黃鉞。

translations.literal: Que returned; the Western Headquarters immediately granted Emperor Wu the yellow battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: Que returned bearing word, and the Western headquarters at once invested Emperor Wu with the yellow battle-axe.

sentences.zh: 蕭穎胄既都督中外諸軍事，論者謂武帝應致箋，域爭不聽，乃止。

translations.literal: Since Xiao Yingzhou had already been Grand Commander of all military affairs within and without, commentators said Emperor Wu ought to submit a memorial of allegiance; Yu contended and would not heed it; it then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: With Xiao Yingzhou already supreme commander, some urged Emperor Wu to submit a formal allegiance; Yuan argued against it and prevailed, and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 郢城平，域及張弘策議與武帝意同，即命眾軍便下，域謀多被納用。

translations.literal: When Ying city was pacified, Yu and Zhang Hongce's plans matched Emperor Wu's intent; he immediately ordered the armies to march down at once; many of Yu's stratagems were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Yingzhou, Yuan and Zhang Hongce counselled in accord with the emperor's aim; he ordered the armies to advance at once, and many of Yuan's proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 霸府初開，為諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When the Hegemon's headquarters first opened, he became Advisory Staff Member.
translations.idiomatic: When the hegemon's headquarters was first established, he became advisory staff officer.

sentences.zh: 天監初，封廣牧縣子、後軍司馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Guangmu and Rear Army Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianjian he was enfeoffed Baron of Guangmu and appointed rear army marshal.

sentences.zh: 出為甯朔將軍、巴西梓潼二郡太守。

translations.literal: He went out as General Pacifying the North and Administrator of the two commanderies Baxi and Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General Pacifying the North and dual administrator of Baxi and Zitong.

sentences.zh: 梁州長史夏侯道遷降魏，魏襲巴西，域固守。

translations.literal: Liangzhou Chief of Staff Xiahou Daoyuan surrendered to Wei; Wei raided Baxi; Yu held firm in defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiahou Daoyuan, chief of staff of Liangzhou, defected to Wei, the Wei struck Baxi; Yuan held the city in a stubborn defense.

sentences.zh: 城中糧盡，將士皆齕草供食，無有離心。

translations.literal: Grain in the city was exhausted; officers and soldiers all gnawed grass for food; none had a heart of departure.
translations.idiomatic: When food ran out the garrison chewed grass to eat, yet none wavered in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 魏軍退，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: When Wei troops withdrew, his rank was advanced to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wei withdrew he was advanced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 于時兵後人饑，域上表振貸，不待報輒開倉，為有司所糾。

translations.literal: At that time after the troops, the people were hungry; Yu submitted a memorial to grant relief; without awaiting reply he immediately opened the granaries; he was impeached by the responsible officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the famine after the war he memorialized for relief grain and, without waiting for approval, opened the granaries; the authorities censured him.

sentences.zh: 上遷域西中郎司馬、輔國將軍、甯蜀太守。
