translations.literal: The emperor transferred Yu to Western Central Commander Marshal, General Assisting the State, and Ningshu Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reassigned him as marshal of the Western Central Commander, General Assisting the State, and administrator of Ningshu.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子子輿。

translations.literal: His son was Ziyu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Ziyu.

sentences.zh: 子輿字孝卿，幼而歧嶷。

translations.literal: Ziyu, style name Xiaoqing, in childhood was precocious.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu (Xiaoqing) showed unusual precocity as a child.

sentences.zh: 五歲讀孝經，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: At five he read the Classic of Filial Piety, his hand never releasing the scroll.
translations.idiomatic: At five he was reading the Classic of Filial Piety without setting the text down.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「此書文句不多，何用自苦？」

translations.literal: Someone said: "This book's sentences are not many—why torment yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked, "That book is short—why drive yourself so hard?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「孝，德之本，何謂不多。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Filial piety is the root of virtue—how can one say it is not much?"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Filial piety is the root of virtue—how can you call that 'not much'?"

sentences.zh: 齊永明末，除州主簿。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongming in Qi, he was appointed Provincial Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Qi's Yongming era he was made provincial chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 時父在梁州遇疾，子輿奔侍醫藥，言淚恒並。

translations.literal: At that time his father in Liangzhou fell ill; Ziyu rushed to attend with medicine, words and tears always together.
translations.idiomatic: When his father fell ill in Liangzhou, Ziyu hurried to his side with medicines, weeping as he spoke.

sentences.zh: 長沙宣武王省疾見之，顧曰：「庾錄事雖危殆，可憂更在子輿。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Changsha, Xuanwu, visiting the sick and seeing this, turned and said: "Recording Secretary Yuan though in peril, what is to be worried about more is in Ziyu."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xuanwu of Changsha, visiting the sickbed, remarked, "The recording secretary may be failing—but it is Ziyu who truly wrings the heart."

sentences.zh: 尋丁母憂，哀至輒嘔血，父戒以滅性，乃禁其哭泣。

translations.literal: Soon he entered mourning for his mother; grief when extreme would bring up blood; his father admonished him about destroying his nature and then forbade his weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his mother's death plunged him into such grief that he vomited blood; his father, fearing he would ruin himself, forbade him to weep.

sentences.zh: 梁初為尚書郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Liang he was a Master of Writing Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Liang he served as a gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 天監三年，父出守巴西，子輿以蜀路險難，啟求侍從，以孝養獲許。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianjian, his father went out to guard Baxi; Ziyu because the Shu road was perilous and difficult, memorialized requesting to attend him, and by filial support obtained permission.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year three his father was posted to guard Baxi; Ziyu petitioned to accompany him down the perilous road into Shu and won leave on grounds of filial duty.

sentences.zh: 父遷甯蜀，子輿亦相隨。

translations.literal: When his father was transferred to Ningshu, Ziyu also followed along.
translations.idiomatic: When his father moved to Ningshu, Ziyu went with him.

sentences.zh: 父于路感心疾，每痛至必叫，子輿亦悶絕。

translations.literal: His father on the road contracted a heart affliction; whenever pain came he would cry out, and Ziyu also would faint.
translations.idiomatic: On the road his father was stricken with heart pains and cried out at every spasm; Ziyu fainted beside him each time.

sentences.zh: 及父卒，哀慟將絕者再。

translations.literal: When his father died, his grief and anguish twice brought him near death.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, twice his mourning nearly killed him.

sentences.zh: 奉喪還鄉，秋水猶壯。

translations.literal: Bearing the coffin home, the autumn waters were still strong.
translations.idiomatic: Bringing the coffin home, he found the autumn rivers still in full spate.

sentences.zh: 巴東有淫預，石高出二十許丈，及秋至，則才如見焉，次有瞿塘大灘，行旅忌之，部伍至此，石猶不見。

translations.literal: In Badong there is Yinyu, its rock rising more than twenty zhang; when autumn came it was then only as if visible; next there is the great rapid of Qutang—travelers fear it; when the company reached here the rock was still not visible.
translations.idiomatic: In eastern Ba lies the Yinyu shoal, whose rock stands some seventy feet above the channel; only in autumn, when the water falls, does it show at all. Beyond it lies the dreaded Qutang rapid. When the funeral party arrived, the rock had not yet emerged and the shoal remained hidden.

sentences.zh: 子輿撫心長叫，其夜五更水忽退減，安流南下。

translations.literal: Ziyu beat his breast and cried out long; that night at the fifth watch the water suddenly receded and diminished; calm current flowed south.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu clutched his chest and wailed. Before dawn the river dropped by itself, and the current bore them safely downstream.

sentences.zh: 及度，水復舊，行人為之語曰：「淫預如襥本不通，瞿塘水退為庾公。」

translations.literal: When they had crossed, the water returned to its former state; travelers made a saying of it: "Yinyu like a bifu—originally impassable; Qutang's water receding—is Lord Yuan's doing."
translations.idiomatic: Once they were through, the waters rose again; travelers made a rhyme of it: "Yinyu like a bale—no passage here; Qutang's ebb—that was Lord Yuan."

sentences.zh: 初發蜀，有雙鳩巢舟中，及至又棲廬側，每聞哭泣之聲，必飛翔簷宇，悲鳴激切。

translations.literal: When first departing Shu, a pair of turtledoves nested in the boat; when they arrived they again perched beside the mourning hut; whenever they heard the sound of weeping, they would fly circling the eaves and rafters, crying mournfully and piercingly.
translations.idiomatic: Two turtledoves had nested in the boat when they left Shu and roosted beside the mourning shed on arrival; at every sound of weeping they wheeled under the eaves, crying in piercing grief.

sentences.zh: 欲為父立佛寺，未有定處。

translations.literal: He wished to build a Buddhist temple for his father but had not yet a fixed site.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to build a Buddhist temple for his father but could not decide where.

sentences.zh: 夢有僧謂曰：「將修勝業，嶺南原即可營造。」

translations.literal: In a dream a monk said to him: "You are about to cultivate supreme merit; the southern slope beyond the ridge may at once be built."
translations.idiomatic: In a dream a monk told him, "You are to build a great merit—establish it on the ridge's southern slope."

sentences.zh: 明往履歷，果見標度處所，有若人功，因立精舍。

translations.literal: At dawn he went to walk and survey; he indeed saw a marked-out place, as if by human labor; he therefore erected a refined abode.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he went to see and found the spot already marked out as if by human hands; there he built a Buddhist cloister.

sentences.zh: 居墓所以終喪，服闋，手足枯攣，待人而起。

translations.literal: He dwelt by the tomb to complete mourning; when mourning was done, his hands and feet were withered and cramped; he needed others to raise him.
translations.idiomatic: He lived by the grave until mourning was complete; when it ended his limbs were withered and stiff, and he could rise only with help.

sentences.zh: 仍布衣蔬食，志守墳墓。

translations.literal: He still wore cloth garments and ate plain food, his will set on guarding the grave mound.
translations.idiomatic: He still wore hemp and ate sparingly, resolved to guard the tomb.

sentences.zh: 叔該謂曰：「汝若固志，吾亦抽簪。」

translations.literal: His uncle Gai said to him: "If you hold firm to your resolve, I too will pull out my hairpin."
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Gai said, "If you hold to this resolve, I too will leave office."

sentences.zh: 於是始仕。

translations.literal: Thereupon he first entered office.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did he take office.

sentences.zh: 雖以嫡長襲爵，國秩盡推諸弟。

translations.literal: Although as eldest son of the main line he inherited the fief, the income of the state stipend he entirely yielded to his younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Though as eldest legitimate heir he inherited the title, he gave every bit of the estate income to his younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 累遷兼中郎司馬。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Concurrent Central Commander Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He rose eventually to concurrent marshal of the Central Commander.

sentences.zh: 大通二年，除巴陵內史，便道之官，路中遇疾。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong, he was appointed Intendant of Baling and went to office by convenience of route; on the road he met with illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year two he was appointed intendant of Baling and set out by the direct route; illness overtook him on the way.

sentences.zh: 或勸上郡就醫，子輿曰：「吾疾患危重，全濟理難，豈可貪官，陳屍公廨。」

translations.literal: Some urged him to enter the commandery for medical treatment; Ziyu said: "My illness is severe and critical; full recovery is hard in reason—how can I be greedy for office and display my corpse in the public yamen?"
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to reach the prefectural seat for treatment; Ziyu said, "I am past recovery—how could I cling to office and die in the government hall?"

sentences.zh: 因勒門生不得輒入城市，即於渚次卒。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered his students not to enter the city at will; he then died on the river islet.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade his retainers to enter the city and died that same day on a sandbar by the shore.

sentences.zh: 遺令單衣帢履以斂，酒脯施靈而已。

translations.literal: His testament ordered plain clothes, kerchief, and sandals for encoffining; wine and dried meat offered at the spirit tablet only.
translations.idiomatic: He left orders to be buried in simple clothes, kerchief, and sandals, with only wine and meat for the funeral offering.

sentences.zh: 鄭紹叔字仲明，滎陽開封人也。

translations.literal: Zheng Shaoshu, style name Zhongming, was a man of Kaifeng in Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Shaoshu (Zhongming) was from Kaifeng in Xingyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 累世居壽陽。

translations.literal: For generations they dwelt in Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: His family had lived in Shouyang for generations.

sentences.zh: 祖琨，宋高平太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kun was Song Administrator of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kun had been administrator of Gaoping under the Song.

sentences.zh: 紹叔年二十餘，為安豐令，有能名。

translations.literal: Shaoshu in his twenties was Magistrate of Anfeng, with a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: In his twenties Shaoshu served as magistrate of Anfeng and won a name for competence.

sentences.zh: 後為本州中從事史。

translations.literal: Later he was Chief Clerk of Personnel in this province.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made provincial personnel officer for his home province.

sentences.zh: 時刺史蕭誕弟諶被誅，台遣收誕，兵使卒至，左右驚散，紹叔獨馳赴焉。

translations.literal: At that time the Inspector Xiao Yan's brother Chen was executed; the court sent to take Yan; military envoys arrived suddenly; those at his side scattered in alarm; only Shaoshu galloped to go there.
translations.idiomatic: When the inspector Xiao Yan's brother Chen was executed, the court sent troops to arrest Yan; his attendants fled in panic, but Shaoshu alone galloped to his side.

sentences.zh: 誕死，侍送喪柩，眾咸稱之。

translations.literal: Yan died; he attended and escorted the coffin; the multitude all praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan was killed, he helped convey the coffin home, and all praised his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 到都，司空徐孝嗣見而異之，曰：「祖逖之流也」。

translations.literal: Arriving at the capital, Minister of Works Xu Xiaosi saw him and marveled, saying: "Of the sort of Zu Ti."
translations.idiomatic: In the capital Minister of Works Xu Xiaosi, meeting him, exclaimed, "A man in the mold of Zu Ti!"

sentences.zh: 梁武帝臨司州，命為中兵參軍，領長流。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang was at Sizhou, he appointed him Central Troops Staff Member, in charge of Changliu.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Wu governed Sizhou, he made Shaoshu central troops staff officer with charge of the Changliu command.

sentences.zh: 因是厚自結附。

translations.literal: Because of this he thickly attached himself in bonds of loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: From that time he bound himself closely to him.

sentences.zh: 帝罷州還都，謝遣賓客，紹叔獨固請願留。

translations.literal: When the Emperor left the province and returned to the capital, he thanked and dismissed his guests; only Shaoshu firmly requested that he wished to remain.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince left his post for the capital he dismissed his retainers; only Shaoshu begged to stay.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿才幸自有用，我今未能相益，宜更思佗塗。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Your talent fortunately has its own use; I now cannot benefit you mutually—you should further consider another path."
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "Your gifts deserve employment, but I cannot advance you here—you ought to seek another patron."

sentences.zh: 固不許。

translations.literal: He firmly would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoshu would not hear of leaving.

sentences.zh: 於是乃還壽陽。

translations.literal: Thereupon he returned to Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: At length he returned to Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 刺史蕭遙昌苦要引，紹叔終不受命。

translations.literal: The Inspector Xiao Yaochang sorely pressed to draw him in; Shaoshu to the end did not accept the commission.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Xiao Yaochang pressed him hard to serve, but Shaoshu refused every commission.

sentences.zh: 遙昌將囚之，鄉人救解得免。

translations.literal: Yaochang was about to imprison him; fellow townsmen rescued and released him, and he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Yaochang nearly had him imprisoned; townsfolk intervened and freed him.

sentences.zh: 及帝為雍州，紹叔間道西歸，補甯蠻長史、扶風太守。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was at Yongzhou, Shaoshu by hidden route returned west and was appointed Chief of Staff of Pacifying the Barbarians and Administrator of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became governor of Yongzhou, Shaoshu stole west by back roads to join him and was made chief of staff for Pacifying the Barbarians and administrator of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 東昏既害朝宰，頗疑於帝。

translations.literal: After the Depraved Emperor of the East had killed the court ministers, he was rather suspicious of the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Donghun murdered the chief ministers, he grew suspicious of the prince of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹叔兄植為東昏直後，東昏遣至雍州，托候紹叔，潛使為刺客。

translations.literal: Shaoshu's elder brother Zhi was Eastern Depraved's Palace Attendant in Waiting; the Depraved Emperor sent him to Yongzhou, ostensibly to visit Shaoshu, secretly making him an assassin.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoshu's elder brother Zhi served Emperor Donghun as palace attendant; Donghun sent him to Yongzhou on the pretext of visiting Shaoshu, secretly to assassinate the prince.

sentences.zh: 紹叔知之，密白帝。

translations.literal: Shaoshu knew it and secretly reported to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoshu learned of the plot and secretly informed the prince.

sentences.zh: 及植至，帝于紹叔處置酒宴之，戲植曰：「朝廷遣卿見圖，今日閑宴，是見取良會也。」

translations.literal: When Zhi arrived, the Emperor at Shaoshu's place set out wine and feasted him, joking to Zhi: "The court sent you to scheme against me—today's leisurely banquet is a fine occasion to be taken."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi arrived the prince hosted a banquet at Shaoshu's quarters and teased him: "The court sent you to plot against me—what better moment for assassination than a leisurely feast?"

sentences.zh: 賓主大笑。

translations.literal: Guest and host laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Host and guest roared with laughter.

sentences.zh: 令植登城隍，周觀府署，士卒器械，舟艫戎馬，莫不富實。

translations.literal: He had Zhi ascend the city wall and ramparts, look all around the government offices—soldiers, weapons, boats and warships, war horses—nothing not rich and ample.
translations.idiomatic: He had Zhi climb the walls and tour the compound—troops, arms, ships, and horses, all in splendid abundance.

sentences.zh: 植退謂紹叔曰：「雍州實力，未易圖也。」

translations.literal: Zhi withdrew and said to Shaoshu: "Yongzhou's real strength—not easy to scheme against."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi withdrew and told Shaoshu, "Yongzhou's strength makes it no easy mark."

sentences.zh: 紹叔曰：「兄還具為天子言之，兄若取雍州，紹叔請以此眾一戰。」

translations.literal: Shaoshu said: "When elder brother returns, fully tell the Son of Heaven for me—if elder brother takes Yongzhou, Shaoshu requests to give battle with this host."
translations.idiomatic: Shaoshu said, "Tell the emperor plainly when you return: if he means to take Yongzhou, I ask only to meet his army in the field."

sentences.zh: 送兄于南峴，相持慟哭而別。

translations.literal: He escorted his elder brother to Southern Xian; they held each other and wept bitterly in parting.
translations.idiomatic: He saw his brother off at Southern Xian, and they clung to each other weeping as they parted.

sentences.zh: 續復遣主帥杜伯符亦欲為刺客，詐言作使，上亦密知，宴接如常。

translations.literal: Subsequently again he sent the commander Du Bofu also intending to be assassin, falsely claiming to be an envoy; the Emperor also secretly knew, and feasted and received him as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Donghun then sent Commander Du Bofu as another assassin under the guise of an envoy; the prince knew this too and entertained him as before.

sentences.zh: 伯符懼不敢發。

translations.literal: Bofu feared and did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: Du Bofu was afraid and never struck.

sentences.zh: 上後即位，作五百字詩具及之。

translations.literal: After the Emperor later took the throne, he composed a five-hundred-character poem fully relating these matters.
translations.idiomatic: After he took the throne, the emperor commemorated the episode in a five-hundred-character poem.

sentences.zh: 初起兵，紹叔為冠軍將軍，改驍騎將軍，從東下。

translations.literal: When they first raised the army, Shaoshu was made Champion General, then changed to Valiant Cavalry General, and followed on the eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: At the first mustering of forces, Zheng Shaoshu was appointed Champion General, then reassigned as Valiant Cavalry General and marched east with the army.

sentences.zh: 江州平，留紹叔監州事，曰：「昔蕭何鎮關中，漢祖得成山東之業；

translations.literal: When Jiang Province was pacified, [the Emperor] left Shaoshu to oversee provincial affairs and said: "In former times Xiao He held Guanzhong, and the Founder of Han accomplished his enterprise east of the mountains;
translations.idiomatic: After Jiang Province was secured, he left Shaoshu in charge of the province and told him: "Long ago Xiao He held Guanzhong, and the Han founder won his realm east of the mountains;

sentences.zh: 寇恂守河內，光武建河北之基。

translations.literal: Kou Xun guarded Henei, and Guangwu laid the foundation of his rule north of the [Yellow] River.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Xun held Henei, and Emperor Guangwu built his foundation in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 今之九江，昔之河內，我故留卿以為羽翼。

translations.literal: Today's Jiujiang is yesterday's Henei — I therefore leave you here as wings.
translations.idiomatic: Jiujiang today is what Henei was then; that is why I leave you here as my supporting wing.

sentences.zh: 前途不捷，我當其咎，糧運不繼，卿任其責。」

translations.literal: If the road ahead is not victorious, I will bear the blame; if grain transport fails, you bear the responsibility."
translations.idiomatic: If the campaign ahead goes ill, the fault is mine; if the grain supply breaks, the fault is yours."

sentences.zh: 紹叔流涕拜辭，於是督江、湘糧運無闕乏。

translations.literal: Shaoshu wept and took leave with a bow; thereafter he supervised grain transport on the Jiang and Xiang, and there was no shortage.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoshu wept as he bowed farewell, then oversaw grain shipments on the Yangzi and Xiang rivers until the army never wanted for supplies.

sentences.zh: 天監初，入為衛尉卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian, he entered [the capital] as Chamberlain for Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianjian reign he entered court as Chamberlain for Attendants.

sentences.zh: 紹叔少孤貧，事母及祖母以孝聞，奉兄恭謹。

translations.literal: Shaoshu was orphaned and poor in youth; he served his mother and grandmother with a fame for filial piety, and attended his elder brother with respect.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoshu lost his father young and grew up in poverty, yet won renown for filial service to his mother and grandmother and for the reverent care he gave his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 乃居顯要，糧賜所得及四方遺餉，悉歸之兄室。

translations.literal: Once he held an eminent post, all grain allotments, gifts received, and tribute sent from the four quarters he turned over entirely to his brother's household.
translations.idiomatic: Once he rose to high office, every grain ration, stipend, and gift sent from across the realm went straight to his brother's house.

sentences.zh: 忠於事上，所聞纖豪無隱。

translations.literal: Loyal in service to his sovereign, the slightest thing he heard he concealed nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal in the emperor's service, he reported even the smallest thing he heard and hid nothing.

sentences.zh: 每為帝言事，善則曰：「臣愚不及，此皆聖主之策。」

translations.literal: Whenever he spoke to the Emperor on affairs, if they went well he would say: "Your servant's dullness cannot compare — these are all the sagacious sovereign's policies."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he discussed policy with the emperor, if matters went well he would say, "I am too dull to deserve credit — these are all Your Majesty's own designs."

sentences.zh: 不善，則曰：「臣智慮淺短，以為其事當如是，殆以此誤朝廷也。

translations.literal: If they went ill, he would say: "Your servant's wisdom and counsel are shallow and short; I thought the matter should be thus — I fear I have thereby misled the court.
translations.idiomatic: If they went badly, he would say, "My judgment is shallow; I thought the matter should be handled this way, and I fear I have misled the court by it.

sentences.zh: 臣之罪深矣。」

translations.literal: Your servant's offense is grave indeed."
translations.idiomatic: My fault is grave indeed."

sentences.zh: 帝甚親信之。

translations.literal: The Emperor held him in very close trust.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor trusted him deeply.

sentences.zh: 母憂去職。

translations.literal: He left office on account of his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 紹叔有至性，帝常使人節其哭。

translations.literal: Shaoshu had utmost nature; the Emperor often sent men to moderate his weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoshu's grief was so extreme that the emperor often sent attendants to urge him to restrain his weeping.

sentences.zh: 頃之，封營道縣侯，復為衛尉卿。

translations.literal: Before long he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yingdao County and again made Chamberlain for Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yingdao and again appointed Chamberlain for Attendants.

sentences.zh: 以營道縣戶凋弊，改封東興縣侯。

translations.literal: Because the households of Yingdao County were depleted and distressed, his fief was changed to Marquis of Dongxing County.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yingdao's registered households were depleted and impoverished, his title was transferred to Marquis of Dongxing.

sentences.zh: 三年，魏圍合肥，紹叔以本號督眾軍鎮東關。

translations.literal: In the third year, Wei besieged Hefei; Shaoshu with his former title supervised all armies garrisoning Dong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when Wei besieged Hefei, Shaoshu retained his former rank and commanded the armies garrisoning Dong Pass.

sentences.zh: 事平，復為衛尉。

translations.literal: When matters were settled, he again became Chamberlain [for Attendants].
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis passed, he again became Chamberlain for Attendants.

sentences.zh: 既而義陽入魏，司州移鎮關南，以紹叔為司州刺史。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Yiyang fell to Wei, Sizhou's seat was moved south of the Pass, and Shaoshu was made Inspector of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yiyang fell to Wei, the seat of Sizhou was moved south of the pass, and Shaoshu was appointed its inspector.

sentences.zh: 紹叔至，創立城隍，繕兵積穀，流人百姓安之。

translations.literal: When Shaoshu arrived, he established walls and moats, drilled troops and stored grain, and displaced people and common folk were settled in peace.
translations.idiomatic: On taking up his post, he built walls and moats, drilled troops, and stockpiled grain until refugees and local people alike were secure.

sentences.zh: 性頗矜躁，以權勢自居，然能傾心接物，多所舉薦。

translations.literal: His nature was rather proud and impetuous, and he took his authority as his station; yet he could give his heart in receiving people and recommended many.
translations.idiomatic: He was somewhat proud and quick-tempered and carried himself as one in power, yet he received others with genuine openness and recommended many men of talent.

sentences.zh: 士亦以此歸之。

translations.literal: Gentlemen also for this reason inclined toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Men of letters and office therefore rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 徵為左衛將軍，至家疾篤，詔於宅拜授，輿載還府。

translations.literal: Summoned as General of the Left Guard — when he reached home his illness was grave; an edict invested him at his residence, and he was carried by litter back to his official mansion.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as General of the Left Guard, but by the time he reached home his illness was severe; an edict appointed him there at his house, and he was carried by litter back to his official residence.

sentences.zh: 中使醫藥，一日數至。

translations.literal: Palace envoys brought medicine several times in a day.
translations.idiomatic: Palace envoys brought medicine several times a day.

sentences.zh: 卒於府舍。

translations.literal: He died in his official residence.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his official residence.

sentences.zh: 帝將臨其殯，紹叔宅巷陋，不容輿駕，乃止。

translations.literal: The Emperor was about to attend his laying-out, but Shaoshu's lane and dwelling were too mean to admit the imperial carriage, so he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to attend his lying-in-state, but Shaoshu's lane was too narrow and his house too humble for the imperial carriage, so the visit was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 詔贈散騎常侍、護軍將軍，諡曰忠。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously awarded Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and Protector-General of the Army; his posthumous name was Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously granted him Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and Protector-General of the Army, with the posthumous name Loyal.

sentences.zh: 紹叔卒後，帝嘗潸然謂朝臣曰：「鄭紹叔立志忠烈，善必稱君，過則歸己，當今殆無其比。」

translations.literal: After Shaoshu's death, the Emperor once said with tears to the court ministers: "Zheng Shaoshu set his heart on fierce loyalty; the good he surely attributed to his lord, faults he took upon himself — today there is scarcely his like."
translations.idiomatic: After Shaoshu's death, the emperor once said tearfully to the court, "Zheng Shaoshu devoted himself to fierce loyalty: credit for what went well he gave to his lord, blame for what went wrong he took on himself — there is scarcely anyone like him today."

sentences.zh: 其見賞惜如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem and cherishing he received.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 子貞嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhen succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 呂僧珍字元瑜，東平範人也。

translations.literal: Lu Sengzhen, courtesy name Yuanyu, was a man of Fan in Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sengzhen, courtesy name Yuanyu, was a native of Fan in Dongping commandery.

sentences.zh: 世居廣陵，家甚寒微。

translations.literal: His family had long dwelt at Guangling; their house was very poor and humble.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long lived at Guangling, in circumstances of great poverty.

sentences.zh: 童兒時從師學，有相工曆觀諸生，指僧珍曰：「此兒有奇聲，封侯相也。」

translations.literal: As a boy studying under a teacher, a physiognomist passing among the students pointed at Sengzhen and said: "This boy has an exceptional resonance — the countenance of enfeoffment and nobility."
translations.idiomatic: While still a boy in school, a physiognomist who examined the pupils pointed at Sengzhen and said, "This child has an extraordinary presence — the look of a man who will be enfeoffed."

sentences.zh: 事梁文帝為門下書佐。

translations.literal: He served Emperor Wen of Liang as a secretariat clerk in the Gatehouse.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the service of Emperor Wen of Liang as a clerical aide in the Gatehouse Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 身長七尺七寸，容貌甚偉，曹輩皆敬之。

translations.literal: He stood seven feet seven inches in height, his appearance very imposing; fellows in the office all respected him.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven feet seven inches tall, with a strikingly imposing bearing, and his colleagues in the office all held him in respect.

sentences.zh: 文帝為豫州刺史，以為典簽，帶蒙令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was Inspector of Yuzhou, he appointed him chief clerk and concurrently Magistrate of Meng.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen served as inspector of Yuzhou, he made Sengzhen his chief clerk and concurrently magistrate of Meng.

sentences.zh: 帝遷領軍將軍，補主簿。

translations.literal: When the Emperor moved on to General Who Leads the Army, [Sengzhen] was made up as chief recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was promoted to General Who Leads the Army, Sengzhen was appointed his chief recorder.

sentences.zh: 祅賊唐宇之寇東陽，文帝率眾東討，使僧珍知行軍眾局事。

translations.literal: The demonic rebel Tang Yuzhi raided Dongyang; Emperor Wen led troops east to attack and had Sengzhen handle the bureau of march affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel Tang Yuzhi raided Dongyang, Emperor Wen led an eastern campaign and put Sengzhen in charge of army administration on the march.

sentences.zh: 僧珍宅在建陽門東，自受命當行，每日由建陽門道，不過私室。

translations.literal: Sengzhen's dwelling lay east of Jianyang Gate; from receiving the command until departure, each day he took the Jianyang Gate road and did not pass by his private rooms.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen's home lay east of Jianyang Gate; from the day he received his orders until he marched, he passed daily along the Jianyang Gate road and never turned in at his own house.

sentences.zh: 文帝益以此知之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen thereby came to know him all the better.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen came to know his character all the better for it.

sentences.zh: 司空陳顯達出軍沔北，見而呼坐，謂曰：「卿有貴相，後當不見減，深自努力。」

translations.literal: Minister of Works Chen Xianda campaigned north of the Han River, saw him and summoned him to sit, saying: "You have the mien of nobility; hereafter you will not diminish — strive deeply for yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Chen Xianda, campaigning north of the Han, saw him, called him to sit, and said, "You have the bearing of a great man; your fortune will only rise — apply yourself with all your strength."

sentences.zh: 建武二年，魏軍南攻，五道並進。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu, Wei troops attacked southward along five routes at once.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Jianwu era, Wei armies invaded from the south along five routes at once.

sentences.zh: 武帝帥師援義陽，僧珍從在軍中。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu led troops to relieve Yiyang; Sengzhen followed in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu led troops to relieve Yiyang, and Sengzhen accompanied the army.

sentences.zh: 時長沙宣武王為梁州刺史，魏軍圍守連月，義陽與雍州路斷。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Xuanwu of Changsha was Inspector of Liang Province; Wei troops besieged for months on end, and the road between Yiyang and Yong Province was cut.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Xuanwu of Changsha was inspector of Liang Province; Wei forces had besieged the city for months, and communications between Yiyang and Yong Province were severed.

sentences.zh: 武帝欲遣使至襄陽，求梁州問，眾莫敢行。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to dispatch an envoy to Xiangyang to seek word from Liang Province; no one dared go.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu wished to send an envoy to Xiangyang to obtain news from Liang Province, but no one dared make the journey.

sentences.zh: 僧珍固請充使，即日單舸上道。

translations.literal: Sengzhen firmly volunteered to serve as envoy and that very day went upstream in a lone boat.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen pressed to go as envoy and that same day set out alone in a single boat.

sentences.zh: 及至襄陽，督遣援軍，且獲宣武王書而反，武帝甚嘉之。

translations.literal: When he reached Xiangyang he urged and sent relief troops, and also obtained the Prince of Xuanwu's letter and returned — the Emperor greatly commended him.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangyang he organized and dispatched relief troops, secured a letter from the Prince of Xuanwu, and returned; Emperor Wu praised him highly.

sentences.zh: 東昏即位，司空徐孝嗣管朝政，欲要僧珍與共事。

translations.literal: When Donghun took the throne, Minister of Works Xu Xiaosi managed court affairs and wished to draw Sengzhen in to work together.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Donghun came to the throne, Minister of Works Xu Xiaosi directed the government and tried to recruit Sengzhen to join him.

sentences.zh: 僧珍知不久當敗，竟弗往。

translations.literal: Sengzhen knew they would soon be ruined and ultimately did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen knew their cause would soon collapse and never went.

sentences.zh: 武帝臨雍州，僧珍固求西歸，得補邔令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took up Yong Province, Sengzhen firmly asked to return west and was appointed Magistrate of Bi.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took charge of Yong Province, Sengzhen pressed to return west and was appointed magistrate of Bi.

sentences.zh: 及至，武帝命為中兵參軍，委以心膂。

translations.literal: When he arrived, the Emperor appointed him military aide of the central corps and entrusted him as backbone and sinew.
translations.idiomatic: On his arrival the emperor appointed him military aide of the central corps and entrusted him as a man of his innermost counsel.

sentences.zh: 僧珍陰養死士，歸之者甚眾。

translations.literal: Sengzhen secretly nurtured warriors willing to die; those who joined him were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen secretly gathered men willing to die for the cause, and very many came to him.

sentences.zh: 武帝頗招武猛，士庶響從，會者萬餘人。

translations.literal: The Emperor greatly recruited bold martial men; scholars and commoners answered the call — those who gathered exceeded ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu also recruited bold fighters, and scholars and commoners alike rallied to him until more than ten thousand had assembled.

sentences.zh: 因命按行城西空地，將起數千間屋為止舍。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered a survey of empty ground west of the city, intending to raise several thousand rooms as lodging.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered a survey of open ground west of the city, planning to build several thousand rooms as barracks.

sentences.zh: 多伐材竹，沈于檀溪，積茅蓋若山阜，皆未之用。

translations.literal: They felled much timber and bamboo, sunk it in Tan Stream, piled thatch covers like hillocks — all unused as yet.
translations.idiomatic: They cut great quantities of timber and bamboo, sank them in Tan Stream, and heaped up thatch roofing like hills — none of it yet put to use.

sentences.zh: 僧珍獨悟其指，因私具櫓數百張。

translations.literal: Sengzhen alone grasped the drift and on his own prepared several hundred oars in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen alone grasped the plan and on his own secretly prepared several hundred oars.

sentences.zh: 及兵起，悉取檀溪材竹，裝為船艦，葺之以茅，並立辦。

translations.literal: When the army rose, they took all the Tan Stream timber and bamboo, fitted them as warships, thatched them with straw — all completed at once.
translations.idiomatic: When the army rose, they took all the timber and bamboo from Tan Stream, fitted them into warships, and thatched them with straw — all finished at once.

sentences.zh: 眾軍將發，諸將須櫓甚多，僧珍乃出先所具，每船付二張，爭者乃息。

translations.literal: As the host was about to march, the generals needed many oars; Sengzhen then produced those he had prepared beforehand, giving two to each boat, and the quarreling ceased.
translations.idiomatic: As the armies were about to march, the generals needed many oars; Sengzhen brought out those he had prepared, gave two to each boat, and the quarreling ceased.

sentences.zh: 武帝以僧珍為輔國將軍、步兵校尉，出入臥內，宣通意旨。

translations.literal: The Emperor made Sengzhen Supporter of the State General and Colonel of Footsoldiers; he went in and out of the bedchamber, conveying intents.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu appointed Sengzhen Supporter of the State General and Colonel of Footsoldiers; he moved in and out of the imperial bedchamber and conveyed the emperor's wishes.

sentences.zh: 大軍次江甯，武帝使僧珍與王茂率精兵先登赤鼻邏。

translations.literal: The main army halted at Jiangning; the Emperor sent Sengzhen and Wang Mao with elite troops to seize Chibi Watch first.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army reached Jiangning, Emperor Wu sent Sengzhen and Wang Mao with elite troops to seize Chibi Watch first.

sentences.zh: 其日，東昏將李居士來戰，僧珍等大破之，乃與茂進白板橋。

translations.literal: That day Donghun's general Li Jushi came to give battle; Sengzhen and the rest routed them thoroughly, then advanced with Mao to Whiteboard Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: That day Donghun's general Li Jushi gave battle; Sengzhen and the others routed him completely, then advanced with Wang Mao to Whiteboard Bridge.

sentences.zh: 壘立，茂移頓越城，僧珍守白板。

translations.literal: They raised ramparts; Mao shifted camp to Yuecheng, Sengzhen held Whiteboard.
translations.idiomatic: They threw up fortifications; Wang Mao moved his camp to Yuecheng while Sengzhen held Whiteboard.

sentences.zh: 李居士知城中眾少，直來薄城。

translations.literal: Li Jushi, knowing the city held few troops, came straight to press the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jushi, knowing the garrison was thin, pressed straight against the walls.

sentences.zh: 僧珍謂將士曰：「今力不敵，不可戰，亦勿遙射。

translations.literal: Sengzhen told the officers and men: "Now our strength does not match theirs — do not give battle, and do not shoot from afar either.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen told his officers and men, "We are too weak to fight now, and you must not shoot from a distance either.

sentences.zh: 須至塹裏，當並力破之。」

translations.literal: Wait until they reach the moat; then we shall combine strength to break them."
translations.idiomatic: Wait until they reach the moat inside the walls; then we shall strike together and break them."

sentences.zh: 俄而皆越塹，僧珍分人上城，自率馬步三百人出其後，內外齊擊，居士等應時奔散。

translations.literal: Before long all crossed the moat; Sengzhen sent men up on the walls and himself led three hundred horse and foot out behind them; inside and outside struck together, and Jushi and the rest fled scattered in their season.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they all crossed the moat. Sengzhen sent men up onto the walls while he himself led three hundred horse and foot around behind them; the defenders struck from within and without at once, and Li Jushi and his men broke and fled on the spot.

sentences.zh: 及武帝受禪，為冠軍將軍、前軍司馬，封平固縣侯。

translations.literal: When the Emperor received the abdication, [Sengzhen was made] Champion General and Major of the Forward Army, enfeoffed as Marquis of Pinggu County.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication, Sengzhen was made Champion General and major of the forward army, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Pinggu.

sentences.zh: 再遷左衛將軍，加散騎常侍，入直秘書省，總知宿衛。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to General of the Left Guard, added Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, entered duty at the Secretariat, and oversaw all palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to General of the Left Guard, given the additional title Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, assigned to duty in the Secretariat, and placed in overall charge of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 天監四年，大舉北侵，自是僧珍晝直中書省，夜還秘書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianjian they launched a great northern invasion; from then Sengzhen was on day duty at the Central Secretariat and returned to the Secretariat at night.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianjian a great northern campaign was launched; from then on Sengzhen stood day duty at the Central Secretariat and returned to the Secretariat at night.

sentences.zh: 五年旋軍，以本官領太子中庶子。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the army turned back; with his former title he headed the Crown Prince's palace aides.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the army withdrew, and he retained his rank while also serving as head of the crown prince's palace staff.

sentences.zh: 僧珍去家久，表求拜墓，武帝欲榮以本州，乃拜南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Sengzhen had been away from home long and memorialized to pay respects at the tombs; the Emperor wished to honor him with his native province and so appointed him Inspector of Southern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen had been away from home for years and memorialized to visit his family's tombs; the emperor wished to honor him with his native province and appointed him inspector of Southern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 僧珍在任，見士大夫迎送過禮，平心率下，不私親戚。

translations.literal: Sengzhen in his post, seeing scholars and officers exceed propriety in escorts and farewells, leveled his heart to lead those below and showed no favoritism to kin.
translations.idiomatic: In office he saw that scholars and officials were lavishing excessive ceremony on his comings and goings; he governed with an even hand and showed no favoritism to relatives.

sentences.zh: 兄弟皆在外堂，並不得坐。

translations.literal: His brothers all [remained] in the outer hall — none might sit [in his seat].
translations.idiomatic: His brothers were kept in the outer hall and were not permitted to sit in his official seat.

sentences.zh: 指客位謂曰：「此兗州刺史坐，非呂僧珍床。」

translations.literal: Pointing to the guest seat he said: "This is the Inspector of Yanzhou's seat — not Lu Sengzhen's couch."
translations.idiomatic: Pointing to the guest seat he said, "This is where the inspector of Yanzhou sits — not Lu Sengzhen's couch."

sentences.zh: 及別室促膝如故。

translations.literal: But in a separate room they sat knee to knee as of old.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in a private room they sat knee to knee as warmly as ever.

sentences.zh: 從父兄子先以販蔥為業，僧珍至，乃棄業求州官。

translations.literal: A son of his father's elder cousin had first made his living selling scallions; when Sengzhen arrived he abandoned the trade to seek a provincial post.
translations.idiomatic: A son of his father's elder cousin had made his living selling scallions; when Sengzhen arrived, the man gave up the trade and sought a post in the provincial administration.

sentences.zh: 僧珍曰：「吾荷國重恩，無以報效，汝等自有常分，豈可妄求叨越。

translations.literal: Sengzhen said: "I bear heavy grace from the state and have no way to repay it — you each have your proper station; how can you vainly seek to climb beyond it?
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen said, "I owe the state a heavy debt of grace and have no way to repay it; you each have your proper place in life — how can you seek to rise beyond it by improper means?

sentences.zh: 當速反蔥肆耳。」

translations.literal: Return quickly to your scallion shop."
translations.idiomatic: Go back to your scallion shop at once."

sentences.zh: 僧珍舊宅在市北，前有督郵廨，鄉人咸勸徙廨以益其宅。

translations.literal: Sengzhen's old dwelling was north of the market; before it stood the supervising clerk's yamen; fellow townspeople all urged moving the yamen to enlarge his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen's old house stood north of the market, with the supervising clerk's office in front of it; townspeople urged him to move the office so his residence could be enlarged.

sentences.zh: 僧珍怒曰：「豈可徙官廨以益吾私宅乎。」

translations.literal: Sengzhen said angrily: "How could one move an official yamen to enlarge my private dwelling?"
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen said angrily, "How could I move a government office to enlarge my private house?"

sentences.zh: 姊適於氏，住市西小屋臨路，與列肆雜。

translations.literal: His elder sister had married into the Shi family and lived in a small house west of the market facing the road, mingled among the rows of shops.
translations.idiomatic: His elder sister had married into the Shi family and lived in a small house west of the market, fronting the road amid rows of shops.

sentences.zh: 僧珍常導從鹵簿到其宅，不以為恥。

translations.literal: Sengzhen often led his full ceremonial guard to her dwelling and did not consider it shame.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen often led his full ceremonial escort to her door and felt no shame in it.

sentences.zh: 在州百日，徵為領軍將軍，直秘書省如先。

translations.literal: After a hundred days in the province he was summoned as General Who Leads the Army, on duty at the Secretariat as before.
translations.idiomatic: After a hundred days in the province he was recalled as General Who Leads the Army and resumed his former duty in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 常以私車輦水灑御路。

translations.literal: He often used his private carriage to haul water and sprinkle the imperial road.
translations.idiomatic: He often used his private carriage to carry water and sprinkle the imperial roadway.

sentences.zh: 僧珍既有大勳，任總心膂，性甚恭慎。

translations.literal: Sengzhen had both great merit and a role as backbone and sinew; his nature was very respectful and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen had won great merit and held a position at the heart of power, yet his nature remained deeply respectful and cautious.

sentences.zh: 當直禁中，盛暑不敢解衣。

translations.literal: When on duty within the forbidden precincts, in fierce summer heat he dared not loosen his garments.
translations.idiomatic: On duty within the palace precincts, he would not loosen his garments even in the height of summer.

sentences.zh: 每侍御坐，屏氣鞠躬，對果食未嘗舉箸。

translations.literal: Whenever he attended the imperial seat he held his breath and bowed his body; facing fruit and food he never once raised his chopsticks.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he attended the emperor at table he held his breath and bowed low; even when fruit was set before him he never once raised his chopsticks.

sentences.zh: 因醉後取一甘食，武帝笑謂曰：「卿今日便是大有所進。」

translations.literal: Once after wine he took one sweet morsel; the Emperor laughed and said: "You have today made great progress indeed."
translations.idiomatic: Once, after drinking, he took a sweet morsel; the emperor laughed and said, "You have made great progress today indeed."

sentences.zh: 祿俸外，又月給錢十萬，其餘賜賚不絕于時。

translations.literal: Beyond salary and emoluments he received a hundred thousand cash per month; other gifts and grants were unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond his salary he received a hundred thousand cash each month, and other gifts and grants never ceased.

sentences.zh: 初，

translations.literal: Earlier,
translations.idiomatic: Earlier,

sentences.zh: 武帝起兵，攻郢州久不下，咸欲走北。

translations.literal: when the Emperor raised the army and besieged Ying Province for long without taking it, all wished to flee north.
translations.idiomatic: when Emperor Wu raised his army and besieged Ying Province for a long time without success, everyone wanted to retreat north.

sentences.zh: 僧珍獨不肯，累日乃見從。

translations.literal: Sengzhen alone would not agree; after several days they were seen to follow [his view].
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen alone refused; only after several days did the others yield to his view.

sentences.zh: 一夜，僧珍忽頭痛壯熱，及明而顙骨益大，其骨法蓋有異焉。

translations.literal: One night Sengzhen suddenly had fierce headache and fever; by dawn his forehead bones grew larger still — his bone configuration seemed to have something extraordinary about it.
translations.idiomatic: One night Sengzhen was suddenly seized by fierce headache and fever; by dawn his forehead had swollen still further, as though the structure of his skull were somehow extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 十年，疾病，車駕臨幸，中使醫藥日有數四。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he fell ill; the imperial carriage visited him; palace envoys with medicine came four times a day or more.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he fell ill; the emperor came in person to visit him, and palace envoys bearing medicine arrived four times a day or more.

sentences.zh: 僧珍語親舊曰：「吾昔在蒙縣熱病髮黃，時必謂不濟。

translations.literal: Sengzhen told kin and old friends: "Formerly at Meng County I had fever sickness and turned yellow; then all were sure I would not survive.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen told his kin and old friends, "Long ago, when I was at Meng County, I had a fever and turned yellow, and everyone was sure I would not recover.

sentences.zh: 主上見語，'卿有富貴相，必當不死'。

translations.literal: The Sovereign said to me, 'You have the physiognomy of wealth and rank — you will surely not die.'
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign told me, 'You have the look of wealth and rank — you will surely not die.'

sentences.zh: 俄而果愈。

translations.literal: Before long I did indeed recover.
translations.idiomatic: Before long I did indeed recover.

sentences.zh: 吾今已富貴，而復髮黃，所苦與昔政同，必不復起。」

translations.literal: I am wealthy and honored now, yet again I turn yellow; the affliction is exactly the same as then — I shall surely not rise again."
translations.idiomatic: I am wealthy and honored now, yet I have turned yellow again; the sickness is exactly the same as before — I shall surely not rise again."

sentences.zh: 竟如言卒于領軍官舍。

translations.literal: In the end it was exactly as he had said: he died at the headquarters residence of the General Who Leads the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the end it happened just as he had foretold: he died at the headquarters residence of the General Who Leads the Army.

sentences.zh: 武帝即日臨殯，贈驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司，諡曰忠敬。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu that same day attended the lying-in-state, posthumously granted him General of Fast Cavalry and Director with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies, and gave the posthumous name Loyal and Respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu came that very day to attend his bier, posthumously enfeoffed him as General of Fast Cavalry with an office equal in ceremony to the Three Excellencies, and gave him the posthumous name Loyal and Respectful.

sentences.zh: 武帝痛惜之，言為流涕。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu grieved and cherished his memory; as he spoke, tears flowed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved deeply for him and wept as he spoke.

sentences.zh: 子淡嗣。

translations.literal: His son Dan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dan succeeded to his line.

sentences.zh: 初，宋季雅罷南康郡，市宅居僧珍宅側。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Song Jiya left his post as Administrator of Nankang, he bought a dwelling and lived beside Sengzhen's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Song Jiya left office as administrator of Nankang commandery, he bought a house and settled next to Sengzhen's home.

sentences.zh: 僧珍問宅價，曰：「一千一百萬」。

translations.literal: Sengzhen asked the price of the house; [Jiya] said: "Eleven million."
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen asked what he had paid for the house. Jiya said, "Eleven million."

sentences.zh: 怪其貴，季雅曰：「一百萬買宅，千萬買鄰。」

translations.literal: Wondering at the expense, Jiya said: "A million to buy the house, ten million to buy the neighbor."
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen marveled at the price. Jiya said, "One million for the house, ten million for the neighbor."

sentences.zh: 及僧珍生子，季雅往賀，署函曰：「錢一千」。

translations.literal: When Sengzhen had a son, Jiya went to congratulate him and on the envelope wrote: "One thousand in cash."
translations.idiomatic: When Sengzhen had a son, Jiya came to offer congratulations and wrote on the gift envelope, "One thousand cash."

sentences.zh: 閽人少之，弗為通，強之乃進。

translations.literal: The gatekeeper thought it too little and would not announce him; only after he pressed hard was he admitted.
translations.idiomatic: The gatekeeper thought the sum too small and refused to announce him; only after Jiya insisted was he let in.

sentences.zh: 僧珍疑其故，親自發，乃金錢也。

translations.literal: Sengzhen suspected there was some reason and opened it himself — it was gold cash.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen suspected some hidden meaning and opened the packet himself: it was gold.

sentences.zh: 遂言于帝，陳其才能，以為壯武將軍、衡州刺史。

translations.literal: He then reported to the Emperor, set forth Jiya's talents, and [Jiya] was made General Who Strengthens Martiality and Inspector of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then spoke to the emperor, praised Jiya's ability, and had him appointed General Who Strengthens Martiality and inspector of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 將行，謂所親曰：「不可以負呂公。」

translations.literal: When about to depart, he said to those close to him: "One must not fail Lord Lü."
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to leave, he told his intimates, "I must not disappoint Lord Lü."

sentences.zh: 在州大有政績。

translations.literal: In the province he achieved great administrative merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the province he won a distinguished record of governance.

sentences.zh: 樂藹字蔚遠，南陽淯陽人，晉尚書令廣之六世孫也。

translations.literal: Le Ai, courtesy name Weiyuan, was a man of Yuyang in Nanyang, sixth-generation descendant of Le Guang, Jin Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Le Ai, courtesy name Weiyuan, was a native of Yuyang in Nanyang commandery and a sixth-generation descendant of Le Guang, who had served Jin as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 家居江陵。

translations.literal: His family dwelt at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: His family lived at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 方頤隆准，舉動醞藉。

translations.literal: Square face and high nose bridge; in bearing he was cultured and restrained.
translations.idiomatic: He had a square face and prominent nose, and carried himself with easy, polished grace.

sentences.zh: 其舅雍州刺史宗愨嘗陳器物，試諸甥侄。

translations.literal: His maternal uncle Zong Que, Inspector of Yongzhou, once displayed various objects and tested the nephew-nephews.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal uncle Zong Que, inspector of Yongzhou, once laid out various objects to test his nephews.

sentences.zh: 藹時尚幼，而無所取，愨由此奇之。

translations.literal: Ai was still young and took none; Que thereby regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Ai was still a boy and took nothing; Que was struck by this and regarded him as exceptional.

sentences.zh: 又取史傳各一卷授藹等，使讀畢言所記。

translations.literal: He also took one volume each from histories and biographies and gave them to Ai and the others, having them read through and report what they remembered.
translations.idiomatic: He also gave Ai and the others one volume each from the histories and had them read through and recite what they recalled.

sentences.zh: 藹略讀具舉，愨益善之。

translations.literal: Ai skimmed through and cited everything; Que thought even better of him.
translations.idiomatic: Ai skimmed the text and recited it all; Que thought still more highly of him.

sentences.zh: 齊豫章王嶷為荊州刺史，以藹為驃騎行參軍，領州主簿，參知州事。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yuzhang of Qi, Xiao Yan, was Inspector of Jingzhou, he made Ai Walking Staff Officer of the Fast Cavalry, chief recorder of the province, and participant in provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yuzhang of Qi, Xiao Yan, served as inspector of Jingzhou, he appointed Ai as a walking staff officer on the Fast Cavalry staff, chief recorder of the province, with a role in provincial administration.

sentences.zh: 嶷嘗問藹城隍風俗、山川險易，藹隨問立對，若案圖牒，嶷益重焉。

translations.literal: Yan once asked Ai about city walls and moats, local customs, mountains and rivers, and what was dangerous or easy; Ai answered on the spot to each question as if consulting maps and registers; Yan esteemed him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Yan once questioned him about fortifications, local customs, and the terrain's strengths and hazards; Ai answered each point at once, as if reading from maps and registers, and Yan came to esteem him all the more.

sentences.zh: 州人嫉之，或譖藹廨門如市，嶷遣覘之，方見藹閉合讀書。

translations.literal: People of the province envied him; some slandered Ai, saying his office gate was like a market; Yan sent to observe and then saw Ai with doors closed, reading.
translations.idiomatic: Men in the province envied him; some slandered him, saying his office gate was as busy as a market. Yan sent someone to look and found Ai behind closed doors, reading.

sentences.zh: 後為大司馬記室。

translations.literal: Later he became recorder of the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as recorder to the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 永明八年，荊州刺史巴東王子響稱兵反，及敗，焚燒府舍，官曹文書一時蕩盡。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongming, Prince Zixiang of Badong, Inspector of Jingzhou, raised troops in rebellion; when defeated he burned the government offices, and all official documents were destroyed at once.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year eight, Prince Zixiang of Badong, inspector of Jingzhou, raised troops in revolt; when he was defeated he burned the government compound and every official record was lost at once.

sentences.zh: 齊武帝見藹，問以西事，藹占對詳敏，帝悅，用為荊州中從事，敕付以修復府州事。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Qi received Ai and questioned him about western affairs; Ai answered with detailed acuity; the Emperor was pleased and made him Middle Aide of Jingzhou, charging him with restoring the prefectural and provincial offices.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Qi received Ai and questioned him about affairs in the west; Ai replied with detailed acuity, and the emperor was pleased. He appointed Ai middle aide of Jingzhou and charged him with restoring the prefectural and provincial offices.

sentences.zh: 藹還州，繕修廨署數百區，頃之咸畢。

translations.literal: Ai returned to the province and repaired several hundred sections of government buildings; shortly all was complete.
translations.idiomatic: Ai returned to the province and repaired several hundred government offices; before long the work was finished.

sentences.zh: 豫章王嶷薨，藹解官赴喪，率荊、湘二州故吏建碑墓所。

translations.literal: When Prince Yuzhang Xiao Yan died, Ai resigned office to attend the funeral and led former officers of Jing and Xiang provinces to erect a stele at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yuzhang Xiao Yan died, Ai left office to attend the funeral and led former officers of Jing and Xiang provinces to erect a stele at the tomb.

sentences.zh: 南康王為西中郎，以藹為諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Nankang became Western Central Commander, he made Ai Advisory Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Nankang became Western Central Commander, he appointed Ai advisory staff officer.

sentences.zh: 蕭穎胄引藹及宗夬、劉坦任以經略。

translations.literal: Xiao Yingzhou brought in Ai together with Zong Que and Liu Tan, entrusting them with strategic planning.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yingzhou brought in Ai along with Zong Que and Liu Tan and entrusted them with strategic planning.

sentences.zh: 天監初，累遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian, by successive promotion he became Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianjian era he rose by stages to Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 初，藹發江陵，無故於船得八車輻，如中丞健步避道者，至是果遷焉。

translations.literal: At first, when Ai left Jiangling, for no reason on the boat he obtained eight carriage-wheel hubs — like a censor's vigorous step yielding the road — and at this he was indeed promoted.
translations.idiomatic: When Ai first left Jiangling, he found for no apparent reason eight carriage-wheel hubs aboard his boat — an omen like a censor striding aside to let others pass — and now he was indeed promoted to that office.

sentences.zh: 性公強，居憲台甚稱職。

translations.literal: By nature upright and forceful; in the Censorate he was very fitting to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and forceful by nature, he proved thoroughly suited to the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 時長沙宣武王將葬，而車府忽於庫失油絡，欲推主者。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Xuanwu of Changsha was to be buried, but the Carriage Bureau suddenly in the storehouse lost an oil-soaked canopy; they wished to investigate the person in charge.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xuanwu of Changsha was about to be buried, the Carriage Bureau suddenly found an oil-soaked funeral canopy missing from its storehouse and meant to fix blame on the keeper.

sentences.zh: 藹曰：「昔晉武庫火，張華以為積油萬石必然，今庫若灰，非吏罪也。」

translations.literal: Ai said: "Formerly when the Jin armory caught fire, Zhang Hua held that accumulated oil of ten thousand piculs made it inevitable; if the storehouse now has ash, it is not the clerks' crime."
translations.idiomatic: Ai said, "When the Jin armory burned, Zhang Hua judged that ten thousand piculs of stored oil made fire inevitable. If this storehouse holds only ash, the clerks are not at fault."

sentences.zh: 既而檢之，果有積灰，時稱其博物弘恕。

translations.literal: Thereupon on inspection they indeed found accumulated ash; the age praised his broad learning and magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: On inspection they indeed found accumulated ash, and men of the time praised his wide learning and generous judgment.

sentences.zh: 二年，出為平越中郎將、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year he went out as General of Pacifying Yue and Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was sent out as General of Pacifying Yue and inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 前刺史徐元瑜罷歸，遇始興人士反，逐內史崔睦舒，因掠元瑜財產。

translations.literal: The former inspector Xu Yuanyu left his post and returned; he encountered a revolt of prominent men of Shixing, who expelled the internal administrator Cui Mushu and thereupon plundered Yuanyu's property.
translations.idiomatic: The outgoing inspector Xu Yuanyu was returning home when he ran into a revolt of local magnates in Shixing; they drove out the internal administrator Cui Mushu and looted Yuanyu's goods.

sentences.zh: 元瑜走歸廣州，借兵於藹，托欲討賊，而實謀襲藹。

translations.literal: Yuanyu fled back to Guangzhou, borrowed troops from Ai, claiming he wished to attack the rebels, but in fact plotted to surprise Ai.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyu fled to Guangzhou, borrowed troops from Ai on the pretext of suppressing the rebels, but in fact meant to strike at him by surprise.

sentences.zh: 藹覺誅之。

translations.literal: Ai perceived this and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Ai saw through the plot and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 尋卒於官。

translations.literal: Soon he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died in office.

sentences.zh: 藹姊適征士同郡劉虯，亦明識有禮訓。

translations.literal: Ai's elder sister was married to the recluse Liu Qiu of the same commandery, who also had keen discernment and ritual teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Ai's elder sister had married the recluse Liu Qiu of the same commandery, a man likewise noted for discernment and moral cultivation.

sentences.zh: 藹為州，迎姊居官舍，三分祿秩以供焉，西土稱之。

translations.literal: When Ai was in the province he welcomed his sister to dwell in the official residence, allotting a third of his salary to support her; the western lands praised this.
translations.idiomatic: While he held the province he brought his sister to live in his official quarters and set aside a third of his salary for her support; the western regions praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 子法才。

translations.literal: His son was Facai.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Facai.

sentences.zh: 法才字元備，幼與弟法藏俱有美名。

translations.literal: Facai, courtesy name Yuanbei, in youth with his younger brother Fazang both had fine reputations.
translations.idiomatic: Facai, courtesy name Yuanbei, won a fine reputation in youth, as did his younger brother Fazang.

sentences.zh: 沈約見之曰：「法才實才子。」

translations.literal: Shen Yue upon seeing them said: "Facai is truly a talented man."
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Yue met them he said, "Facai is a man of real talent."

sentences.zh: 為建康令，不受奉秩，比去將至百金，縣曹啟輸台庫。

translations.literal: As Magistrate of Jiankang he did not accept his official salary; by the time he left it neared a hundred in gold; the county clerks memorialized to forward it to the imperial treasury.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Jiankang he refused his salary; by the time he left office nearly a hundred in gold had accumulated, and the county office reported it for transfer to the imperial treasury.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘉其清節，曰：「居職若斯，可以為百城表矣」。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu praised his integrity and said: "To hold office thus — he may serve as a model for a hundred cities."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu praised his integrity and said, "To govern like this is to set an example for a hundred cities."

sentences.zh: 遷太舟卿，尋除南康內史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand Mariner; soon he was appointed Internal Administrator of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Mariner and soon appointed internal administrator of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 恥以讓奉受名，辭不拜。

translations.literal: Ashamed to accept appointment in name while declining the grant salary, he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was ashamed to take the title while refusing the stipend that went with it and declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 歷位少府卿，江夏太守，因被代，表求便道還鄉。

translations.literal: Through successive posts as Vice Director of the Palace and Administrator of Jiangxia, because he was replaced he memorialized requesting convenient route to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as vice director of the palace workshops and administrator of Jiangxia; when he was replaced he memorialized asking leave to return home by the most direct route.

sentences.zh: 至家，割宅為寺，棲心物表。

translations.literal: On reaching home he carved his dwelling into a temple and settled his mind beyond worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Once home he turned part of his house into a temple and gave his heart to life beyond the world.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 法藏位征西錄事參軍，早亡。

translations.literal: Fazang held the post of Recorder under the General Who Pacifies the West; he died young.
translations.idiomatic: Fazang had held the post of recorder on the staff of the General Who Pacifies the West and died young.

sentences.zh: 子子雲，美容貌，善舉止。

translations.literal: His son was Ziyun, handsome in appearance and fine in bearing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ziyun was handsome and graceful in manner.

sentences.zh: 位江陵令，元帝承制，除光祿卿。

translations.literal: He held the post of Magistrate of Jiangling; when Emperor Yuan assumed authority under imperial commission, [Ziyun] was appointed Director of Imperial Entertainment.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Jiangling; when Emperor Yuan assumed power under imperial commission, Ziyun was appointed Director of Imperial Entertainment.

sentences.zh: 魏克江陵，眾奔散，呼子云。

translations.literal: When Wei captured Jiangling, the crowd scattered in flight, calling Ziyun.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei forces took Jiangling the people fled in panic, calling for Ziyun.

sentences.zh: 子雲曰：「終為虜矣，不如守以死節。」

translations.literal: Ziyun said: "In the end we shall be captives; better to hold firm and die for integrity."
translations.idiomatic: Ziyun said, "We shall end as captives in any case; better to hold our ground and die with honor."

sentences.zh: 遂僕地，卒於馬蹄之下。

translations.literal: Thereupon he threw himself to the ground and died beneath horses' hooves.
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself to the ground and was trampled to death under the horses' hooves.

sentences.zh: 論曰：張弘策惇厚慎密，首預帝圖，其位遇之隆，豈徒外戚云爾。

translations.literal: The evaluation says: Zhang Hongce was sincere, generous, careful and close; first to share in the Emperor's design; his eminence in position and favor — was it merely as an outer relative?
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Zhang Hongce was sincere, steadfast, careful, and discreet; he was among the first to share in the founding design, and his rank and favor were hardly owed to kinship alone.

sentences.zh: 至如太清板蕩，親屬離貳，纘不能協和蕃嶽，克濟溫、陶之功；

translations.literal: As for when Taiping was in turmoil, kin divided against kin, Zuan could not harmonize the frontier princes and complete the achievement of Wen and Tao;
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the Taiping years brought chaos and kin turned against kin, Zhang Zuan could neither rally the frontier princes nor bring to completion an achievement like that of Wen Jiao and Tao Kan;

sentences.zh: 而苟懷私怨，以成釁隙之首。

translations.literal: yet he harbored private resentment and became the first opening of strife.
translations.idiomatic: instead he nursed private resentments and became the first to open the breach of civil war.

sentences.zh: 風格若此，而為梁之亂階，惜乎！

translations.literal: Character like this, yet to be the stairway of Liang's disorder — regrettable!
translations.idiomatic: With a character such as this, to stand at the threshold of Liang's ruin — how regrettable!

sentences.zh: 庾域、鄭紹叔、呂僧珍等，或忠誠亮藎，或恪勤匪懈，締構王業，皆有力焉。

translations.literal: Yu Yu, Zheng Shaoshu, Lu Sengzhen and others — some loyal and bright in devotion, some assiduous without slackening — in knitting together the royal enterprise, all had strength.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yu, Zheng Shaoshu, Lu Sengzhen, and the rest — some loyal and shining in devotion, others tireless in diligence — all lent real strength to the founding of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 僧珍之肅恭禁省，紹叔之勤誠靡貳，蓋有人臣之節矣。

translations.literal: Sengzhen's reverent respect within the forbidden quarter, Shaoshu's earnest loyalty without duplicity — surely they had the integrity of ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen's reverence within the palace precincts and Shaoshu's steadfast loyalty showed the true bearing of ministers.

sentences.zh: 藹雖異帷幄之勳，亦贊雲雷之業，其當官任事，寵秩不亦宜乎。

translations.literal: Although Ai differed in merit within the curtain, he also assisted the cloud-and-thunder enterprise; his holding office and handling affairs — were favor and rank not fitting?
translations.idiomatic: Le Ai, though he did not share their merit at the center of counsel, still aided the founding enterprise; that he held high office and received favor was surely no less than fitting.
